name: Kristan Hawkins
subject: Not now, not ever.
body:
A governor just told pro-life states their laws don't count

*|MC_PREVIEW_TEXT|* | | |
---
| | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)
Dear Pro-Life Friend,

A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana.

Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her.

Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were:
_“I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.**Not now, not ever.** ”_
The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don’t count.

**That’s what abortionist “shield laws” do.** They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label!

Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m President of Students for Life of America. I’ve spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I’ve never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen.

The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back.

Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down.

**I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America.**

For years, we’ve been told abortion is now “a state issue.”

_If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,_one mailbox at a time__.

Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I’ve carried with me for most of my adult life:

_“I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?”_

I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today.

[Will you make a generous tax-deductible gift right away to help us stand with the pro-life states in this fight](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)**?**

The Solicitor General is the federal government’s lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that’s John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands.

That means the Trump Administration’s voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation.

President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. **If that’s true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government’s help protecting the laws their people passed.**

And right now, they aren’t getting enough of it.

The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills.

That’s why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what’s being shipped through the mail.

Louisiana’s attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn’t list the prescriber or a single risk.

Louisiana’s attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: _**“It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes.”**_

And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state’s pro-life laws.

Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year.

_And the women who take these deadly pills?_

A study from the _Ethics & Public Policy Center _recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. **That’s at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug’s own label!**

Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . .

Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years.

When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations.

Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation’s water and the endangered species that live in it.

And now, we’re preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We’ve also done this before and seen the impact.

On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up.
[](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm) _Roe v. Wade_ had been called “settled law” for 48 years.

Eight months later, it was gone.

I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. **But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible.**

This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand.

But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills.

[So please make your most generous tax-deductible contribution right now](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)**:**
**> >> $25** puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop.
**> >> $50** covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits.
**> >> $100** launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials.
**> >> $250** helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out.
**> >> $500** helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event.
Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind.
Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do.

Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her.

For Life,

Kristan Hawkins
President, _Students for Life_

P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. The federal government’s voice could make all the difference. We’re preparing a legal brief to stand with them, and I need your help to finish this fight. [Please give $500, $250, $100, $50, or $25 right away](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyU0MGu2yAQheGnwbtYMNhDvGBRKfIu3XZpERg7qBgsGCfq21epeh_grn_p6NP5dV_uLqaYt59uJ1t5XWpbcuFc3rkwvaguIAEvSl0kLs5zfNEyuC7Y4INTviOrzKQnHBCm7mkfRl-luSo0Gt20ymkkZZDCoEIIGLCL9rOnlESltISxB4TwGNFIgyMOgGKQLlHlvtJxPlL0LrNrv9dSPfW-7F2yT-ajCf1DwCxgbuTPSn3jM1Dmtpaa4kp9qZuA-XCXcrKvf4SeW_VC32g_qgDc2xaD0DdAJcEcTgCevC_e7YeLW_6U_86vUjJTZqFvldeu2nC8Y0qxoRGD3HYX0z8df-PEl4W_AQAA___NLHvm)**.**

clean_body: A governor just told pro-life states their laws don't count |MCPREVIEWTEXT| | | | | | Dear Pro-Life Friend, A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana. Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her. Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges. New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were: “I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.Not now, not ever. ” The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don’t count. That’s what abortionist “shield laws” do. They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label! Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this. My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m President of Students for Life of America. I’ve spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I’ve never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen. The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back. Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down. I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America. For years, we’ve been told abortion is now “a state issue.” If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,one mailbox at a time. Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I’ve carried with me for most of my adult life: “I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?” I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today. ? The Solicitor General is the federal government’s lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that’s John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands. That means the Trump Administration’s voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation. President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. If that’s true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government’s help protecting the laws their people passed. And right now, they aren’t getting enough of it. The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills. That’s why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what’s being shipped through the mail. Louisiana’s attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn’t list the prescriber or a single risk. Louisiana’s attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: “It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes.” And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state’s pro-life laws. Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year. And the women who take these deadly pills? A study from the Ethics & Public Policy Center recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. That’s at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug’s own label! Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . . Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years. When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations. Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation’s water and the endangered species that live in it. And now, we’re preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We’ve also done this before and seen the impact. On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up. Roe v. Wade had been called “settled law” for 48 years. Eight months later, it was gone. I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible. This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand. But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills. : >> $25 puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop. >> $50 covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits. >> $100 launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials. >> $250 helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out. >> $500 helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event. Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind. Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do. Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her. For Life, Kristan Hawkins President, Students for Life P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. The federal government’s voice could make all the difference. ## Dow Sheds 1,800 Points in AI Stock Rout
The Dow [plunged more than 1,800 points](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAUhJ8Gd1j8-7qgSOPupk1pYThcyGLjwIlX-_aRN3mDdEdnRp9m5sfn-ulyycfXd7eDxVjXA569ACK0NbpyS7trD8C-1X3D1MBhXwUThnJOmVmdx3zByodgI4AAOYDl0yxnoyamh2SjNJsG7bwArhlskw96k2BmJrz6YDBke-M4Z4ZzyZUct6DnyAN8iGAUi54oBiFjbePPmg9MEMurXtBGX_eh2IR4diK_EbEQscR8uMPD-HKp1ttBxPKvARFLyRcQsXSs_kH_vinW4F4U0-_W7-OoF-wbNKppqE_aT6oZo4frwf2iNRfacodOfconfXM65YorOc-ajQn3MjQbzmcuJXczEcW-dpfLOyv-38KXFX8CAAD__3KEkmE) yesterday, or 3.4%, wiping out Wednesday's 1,569-point post-election rally in a single session. The S&P 500 fell 4.3%, and the Nasdaq dropped 5.4%, the worst day for all three since April 2025. The Nasdaq is now in correction territory, down more than 10% from its October record. Chip stocks took the hardest hit, with the semiconductor index [falling 12%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3ymzAQR08juvXoA7ApVKSh-6dNyQhpZZQIiWgXe3z7DMkRUr-dt795P76WL5dyKs_vbkfLsS4F35SRGdsSXb7Q7tovZFrrvvLW0DEtWuoRlAI5Ls5zeuGiumAjokbToVX3yUxjf5dDt1lp4t0MHuU0TIPqcYqjNGji6uPDD4--S_bSKSVHpYzqzW0NwxRVwIcOYy-jF73EkLi228-aCm8Y86e-sN183btsN-aDhPkm9Cz0XD5HJb6Q0PMlFnpWSuhZDkLP60mpINF16Ci433DkszyRIBWu4Gtr6DnVAoytXT8_4AgC7vBOheBfACwQHDvwWBgbgUvwTK4wQTtpA65AjDtc_erJQs9ds-F4p5wTjXfRy-fuUv47n_8v-svqPwEAAP__db-ZSw) for its worst day since March 2020 and Nvidia, Broadcom, and Micron each shedding 9% or more. Investors fear the Democrats' victory in the midterms will slow the AI data center buildout that has powered the AI boom. Voters backed limits on or outright rejected AI projects in 40 of 41 local ballot measures Tuesday, and Sen. Bernie Sanders has called for a national moratorium. Wall Street's "fear gauge" [jumped more than 60%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb_GdCDPYOylcPEaun1tSmTsYXHW4BWegPbvI5JPSH2kc3XPx328u5ji9vjvVrI853GjsyRipn2cXbrQ6vYncZnyOvGyk-MyokRdA9RSj85zPGiEKtiZCKmtyILp214rI7tqsQhhmgwpY-jWhWBapI4keFABtOqpivbSAUgN0IJqmyl0_QyBbhi0krMXSlKInPfmM8eNF5rTOx-0Nz6vVbIL86uI9p_AQeBwnmfjt8lfUOBwqQUOAAIHqQQOhbN_1r-fas7BvesUD6q_XsExlWbhNVW7Da8zphSLNkLJx-pi-lnjvzU6LH4HAAD__zApesI) to its highest level since March, and everyday investors sold stocks at their fastest pace since the start of the pandemic. Jobs numbers come out this morning.
## Bomb Hoaxes Ground Flights Across Europe
Bomb threats hit [at least 25 flights](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3O2zAMQE8jbwz049j1oCFF4e0rWnToaDAWFauRLUNiIvT2hYreoCsfQfC9nx_LB4YYjsdX3MmyT8tBtURiprx4jA3tmJ_E5Z72O2-ZkMuipR5AKZDDgiuHNy2qc9YTaTIdWTVOZhr6UV67zY7jgKORE2pC30-rGkaDKJW_9gYnJ7tg2zml5KCUUb253N118srRJ-2GXvpV9JJc4JQvv1I4eCMff6c35cua9i7ajfkswtyEnoWea62XvRyNCT3TAa8i9NyshJ4Tb5TbEr4JkofmBP-kwIWSXycXQIZIWBj0FXwMj63N1pxKAXrldBLUDRk4wfNIVegZM9xu-vHte6-EmdManDBfPreqVMsPymeXrTtriDGUYRS9fOwY4t_3-f-iv63-EwAA__99V5hh) across Europe yesterday, forcing emergency landings, diversions, and fighter-jet escorts from Ireland to Bulgaria. No explosives were found on any plane. French warplanes redirected an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome and escorted it to a military base in Normandy, while Italian, Croatian, and Bulgarian jets [escorted other flights](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd45gcHAoKLZxl223tLAZwuxiY8EkUf5-5af3B6-dMzrSuX_u891Tpv3x22_oOJZ5x3fLyIx1jj6faPP1H3JbyrZwqui5zSDB9Er10sx-ZXrhrLrgIiKg7tCp0WprhlFeu-Qg6iuuZpBmlFYqsHADq2Vc7aJC8LIjd-qUkkYprQZ9WcLVRhXwBsEMMq5ikBiIS738LbRzwpg_5YX1spatyy4xH03oXwImARMnTJTzyQRMR8m0fs5z9Xs7SmXPVHYB05nTf_f0MdMjcR-o1edxPrQen7UcKGDqqgvHm3KmZkYxyMfm6Uvf8c8Gezn4HwAA___IYoIM) operated by Finnair and Ryanair. It was the second wave this week, and it follows a run of other disruptions across Europe, including hackers who sabotaged supermarket freezers and tried to [cook French blood banks](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAUhJ8GOiPbgIHCxW2229umRP45Xpw1Njo-WbRvH5EiL5BuNJ80mpmP-3o3McX8-G920BTKmuGsCYgA12DShXaDT6Bqy25pQzBUV8mlYkIwrlbjKL5gFa3XAUBC34IW09Ivapj42G56mcUy96MPSxhhUlI55WfPZ8lHBY4PbdRXnBBcCdGLoe-sH5cgPMzSq4EH1wwcfKSC3WeJmTYI6V1egJ0re5v0RnTUpv_XyFsjb-d5dtm6a8bFL6dg8o28BTTZwa9g7m0BDZFxT2ZTKZ5Zk58MIWB8XKRgZdXsR4LKDiz-y1Fl6LJRfBr42KL2xxlTilVNzcAfu4nppxP97cmXlt8BAAD__9mriq4) by cranking storage fridges to extreme temperatures. Britain's transport secretary called them "malicious hoax threats," and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the U.S. is [tracking the incidents](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb_GdKAZ23iXwsVr6Pa1KZHB48WJwSt7AsrfR0T5g9RHOlfnvj2mh4sp7s__biPLIU87nTURM5UpuHShzZUP4jrnbea1kOM6SZCmRWzBTG7heNCEjbeBSJJqyOJtUIPRN-ib1Tq_KINqkKRAg8Je-b6HAPruYDBqbqK9dIhgEBVq1c2-HwJ6uktvNIRFaCAfOZfuPcedVwrpKx9UuiVvTbIr86sK9U_IUcjxPM9u2eflgkKOl1rIEVHIEXohxyuj_e1oQ4rPlWtLnyW_qFt5S02x_nXGlGI1N6HhubmYfpb4b_8cVn4HAAD__22geGw) with European partners. Officials say it's too early to know whether the threats are linked.
## Democratic Socialist Wins L.A. Mayor Race
Los Angeles City Council member Nithya Raman [unseated Mayor Karen Bass](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGu4yAQheGnwR0Rg228Lii2cZdtt7TGMAR2wUQwSpS3v_J9hVv_0ied8_e-3zHldD7-YCHLoe4nvXsmZmp7wHylgu0_cT9qOTg2Qu67VtpIAKnMjo7Ti3YYvA1EmsaBLCzruJppUfMQLS0EiIsxi5q9AXCzCXQY7ZT26nDzkOzFASgDMMI03g4_rwE8_dLeTCo4MSnyiWu7_avp5Eghf-qL2s3VMmQbmZ9djL-F3oTeOFJMOV9N6C3WQtciobfOyCTfyC4KvRmY1hkWeSaOH5QNC54y1y7xfFCmLgt-ahN6G5r1z3fKOXWziEk9CqZvfeCf_fWy-isAAP__6aiAHA) after one term, and Bass conceded Thursday morning with Raman holding a lead of about 3 points. Raman, 45, is a member of the Democratic Socialists of America, making her the city's first socialist mayor. Her win means democratic socialists will now run New York City, Washington, D.C., and Los Angeles. Bass never recovered from criticism of her performance during the January 2025 Palisades fire, which killed 12 people and destroyed thousands of homes while she was in Ghana for a presidential inauguration. Raman hammered Bass on homelessness and housing costs, and the mayor countered that her challenger was "[not ready for primetime](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDuu2zAQRVdDdTT4kaingkUadS9tSmFEjqzJ48cgBxa8-8DeQuoDXJx7_nxv30CJyv03ZPR81K3g1RMyY9sOSG-Uof0g973mnc-GwH0zyjiptVRug8D0xE0P0R-IBu2AXs-LXdw4q2k4PUQ7RQMBlTMhzHZe9mkCu0eYnAvz10D-Pae1clpbPdrbHqfl0BG_THSjOoIYFUbi2m5_KxU-8Uiv-sR2CzUPyZ_Mjy7sL2FWYdbrum5lD-8bby7M-qiJmEIXZv14Y8LAVIswayE-XyAbZCgy1S6h3DFhlxletcmLioyYa2jAFGSvgSBRZ_kDDYvcoXfZQgGnrJ2Xofn4uCgl6m4Wo7pnoPRx5P8r-_TmXwAAAP__NBeQdQ)." Raman, a former urban planner born in India, had endorsed Bass before launching a late bid in February. She takes over a city preparing to host the 2028 Summer Olympics.

## [Want to stay strong after 40? (never eat this "health" food)](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2K4zAUBeCnkbsYXUmWrULFQvDCQlJkiy2Nfq5i7chxkG9i5u0HzytM_R3OgfPvMl1cLvlxv7oFLaV1euC-FSTCOiVXDlpc_UDa_Lp4mis62ibBhT4BnLieXKD8xgmaaBOiQNmghd5Io1XPu2a2MkDwXOIQMBhlkvOmE6CN6wJ6N4Qm26MOgGsACUq2PnYmQcRBRK14CkxxjJnW2v5f84NmTOVzfWNtw7o0xc5Ez43JX0yMTIz7vrdLrE-kg5kYb7_76_XMxKihG__8vR0xOb5yZPIMYuiY0NvLA5PnvjeqqTY-91xK3nTPFL8vLpfvIfrZPW8rvgIAAP__WkN2jw)
According to a leading nutrition expert and former surgeon, there's a handful of popular "health foods" that do nothing to stop age-related muscle and joint decline.

One of these foods is even praised as a "superfood" for aging adults, yet it can actually do more harm than good.

### Urgent Senate Update: A New Day
This week, Marylanders and Americans across the country made their voices heard loud and clear. They've rejected the politics of cruelty and of corruption, and everything that has brought us: an economy that is crushing American families and a government that's lost its moral compass and forgotten who it answers to.

The billionaires who tried to buy this election failed, because no amount of money can hide from the American people the damage that has been done. They felt it for themselves in the checkout line, at the gas pump, and in their healthcare bills. They saw it on the streets of Minneapolis and in communities across the country where children were snatched on their way home from school. They saw it in the atrocities carried out around the world in their name.

The American people said enough is enough. They are now demanding a new kind of politics: a politics for the people. So now it's our turn. Voters are giving Democrats a chance, and it's on us to earn their trust.

We must earn it by taking on the powerful and corrupt interests, by ending finger-in-the-wind politics, and by delivering real results for the American people. That means a kitchen-table agenda that puts more money in the pockets of American workers and lowers the costs that are crushing American families. It means rooting out the rampant corruption and lawlessness of this Administration. It means ending the war in Iran. And it means replacing cruelty with decency and a moral compass at home and around the world.

As we begin this work, we cannot afford to get pulled into the superficial debates that too often consume Washington. This was not an election about right versus left. It was an election about right versus wrong. It was not an election about moderates or progressives. It was an election about whether our government works just for those at the very top, or answers to We the People.

We must also refuse to accept a false choice about whether this election was about the economy or our democracy. We do not have to pick one or the other. Voters have made clear that they understand this is one fight. We cannot fix what's broken in our economy without confronting what's broken in our democracy, and we cannot expect our democracy to endure without fixing what's broken in our economy.

I'm proud to continue the fight for the promise of an economy and a democracy that answer to us all.

This victory belongs not to any part of the party, but to all of you and to the American people everywhere who kept their faith in our country through the darkest days of the last two years. You refused to be silenced. You stood up for our Constitution, for our democracy, for our better angels, and for each other, even when Washington did not. This victory is yours.

Thank you for reminding us of who we are as a country and what is possible when Americans set their minds to it. Thank you for leading us to this point. Now it's up to all of us to deliver.

As always, I'll keep working to deliver for communities across Maryland and make sure your voices continue to be heard in Washington.
Onwards, Chris Van Hollen

## Hinojosa Names Transition Team
Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa named a bipartisan transition team Thursday at her first [post-election press conference](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpCAYhJ8GMyxARQ0ILjGbSy-0mJ9f5RbBgn_GmbffcpJ9gE27q7_q7n-3-WZ98HH9a3c09FrSHPEsAYkwzw7xwBAee3mUA4F8hEeh5N6zEkpzKbnQswXyT5xl5cxduFFWaGQ_NqPWbaOrzSxoWwQHXWs73QA0g-pBjMMdht51w1h5c9GkFFoqIRpRD53tFtW1EvrBOrWwVqDzlHJNGxK-bFnCOz0x15D2KpiN6Cis-cPUxNR0nmf9RWW_TKamaw5T0yfGjxQ8efgR1gsTU-YYEIivPlq--Zj-p2I5Jb6l4PjicyF-ZCyFQ4oLZoyATE1VNu44fQi-6J61Yt2tD59S9Msvn0Z9BwAA__-obo04) in Austin, two days after defeating Gov. Greg Abbott. Former [Republican lawmaker](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGStCAQRk-jGRagg05A8Cdm86cbWgiNsoW0Be04c_stZ4-w-fdeve6vx_QwIYa0_DcbaHp5nBKcJQIR5MkB7BDjsZWj7GApJHsUQveeJJeKCcG4moyl8IRJ1E7P3N1FDVr09_auVNeqetVOtHLo3TxzGIySfvbSmMEJ6Hor-qGrg75sQnAlJOctb4abuXl564TtB-OkrzoOLhDmhlYgeJni4xufkBuLWx31SrSXqv1XybGS43mejceXVCtesekaVXK8zqrk-MHZctEJM4MIltgSkmFrSPiNxbAVo2M-5EJsx0K_m4CJXQpmMXnIkCwwcxQKqc7a7WeIMRTVVx1fNhPip4z--NCnlj8BAAD__724j-k) Ernest Bailes and building trades union leader Ryan Pollock will co-chair the team, with 23-year government veteran Joe Madden as executive director. "_I am going to be a governor for all of Texas_ ," Hinojosa said. Hinojosa said Abbott has been "gracious" and promised a smooth handoff. Asked about Republican lawmakers seeking to check Democrats' power before January, she said voters "want change" and urged both parties not to "get in the way." The Brownsville native also asked Texas Parks and Wildlife to [hold off on any action](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAQRb8Gs56CVhkNCDYhe5tuaCE0T3YQLGHGeX-_xfzC5qf73nv-fC1fJsSQvn-bnVR9-7wkukqkWulcHNFBMT738iwH2RqSfZaa3c-CHCUIAVwuxtbwokV0Tq3czaIjJe5zP0s59LLb1DAONAkvyQs-4jT3VuJd8JlWKew6zF1Q7ZsQXArkvOe3aTSjx3EQ9j4Zh54NnFyo-bzVjSq9TfHxJ7_ovNm8d1FttR6F9b8Yaob6uq6bjcE-cMutbWoUQ912MdSfe4a6ZTLUQjDUfGSot5Dy31wMmPIo8MHgMOejgEkOrhBdDJ6gZthydJC9h5xgzdaA3YI1EBvXbOQEZg8OymEsvcHmZOlMLbQ7lTuuEGMo8s4G_r2bED8r6n_Kfyn8FwAA__-ZSZre) involving about 1,300 acres of public land near Boca Chica Beach and SpaceX's Starbase. A draft commission agenda had listed the land's possible transfer before the item was dropped.
## Democrats Eye Education Changes
Democrat state Sen. Sarah Eckhardt of Austin unseated Republican Comptroller Don Huffines by roughly 6 percentage points Tuesday, becoming the [first Democrat to run](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upSAURp9GOww_ip6CYhq7O-2UZl_YKhkEAls95-0n3leY_svK-tafr-ULfPBx-w0HGnqvaYl414BEWBaHmDGE86hnzWjJR3tWSu6zSC41E4JxvYAlf-EiWme-uXuJFo0YX-qlda90uxuhBjXZfupHLgYhp0Hg-N2jWtUwgebQevPQhOBaSM4V76YBhlUOvbDjBE6uTc_ReUqlox0J31DX8EkXls6mow1mJ8q1Ub8aOTdyvu-7W9Nb6j09svEZNXJ-bjVydngkW4BYhQI7Q_t3h-KIrcHnyn7gzKYjU0khYGEVgVg-iXzcWCUgZFc67Y6F5ZK2Agc7o8PCIt6s2nKSj5-2GJdvH4Kvemx6vh3gw48s_Wfjy8h_AQAA__9geJZU) the state's checkbook since 1999. Eckhardt argued against Education Freedom Accounts, the state's $1 billion school-choice program, on the Senate floor, but says she'll "[vigorously follow the money](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGypCAURL9GMyxAxTEg2MRsNt3QYuAqbCHXgqvO_P0r5xde3qfrdP97zk8TYkjrX7OBpveCc4KrRCCCPDuAHWI8tnKUHSyFZI9C6D6z5FIxIRhXs7EUTphF7fSLu1HUoMUwtqNSXatqr0fFF2k59C87mK4V_QhWta1y0Pd84KoO-m4TgishOW958-hNv8i-E3Z4GCeXquPgAmFuyAPB25QlfvCE3Fjc6qg90V6q9k8lp0pO13U1C76l8njLpjtUyemeVcnpi7P1phNmtoZkmA8J_2MxrFiPGNmJh_WQCytkTGbgDmsoYGLWm7RCqbN2-xViDEUNVcfXzYT4daFfXnhq-RMAAP__LRiJ7w)" once she takes office in January. The founder of a private school in Houston says enrollment has jumped 200% since the program launched. Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has vowed to "repair the damage of the Texas voucher scam." But the program is [written into state law](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ8GOwygohYU19jttVcahJ-VLIqBH919-4v3CldPZibf9_OYH9oHvz-_9QYK3y7OO1w5ACKk2QIcEELZcskHGPS7KRmj_cyCCUk5p0zO2qA_YeaVVQuzI69A8X5sRinbRlar6t3Q9nyQbLGDs50bwch-aJbRaNaabqm8utc4Z5ILxhpWD53unOhabvpBW-FIy8B6jKnGFRDeOrvwiSek2sStCmpFPDJpvoiYiJiu66pfb73fIRHTjUPEBLYYjT7uREwWtmiSxkxRhxd1BUsCGh3NZo0x0DMWs0K6a1VS9rh8CD7LnrTsuWkf_m7xn7ZOJX4DAAD__zn-gY8), and only legislators can undo it. Control of the State Board of Education, which sets what Texas schools teach and approves charter schools, comes down to [one undecided seat](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGunDAQheGnMZ2RZwAvFC7S0N20KZHxDIsVgxEelnvfPtp9hdRH-nT0__mavnxMcX_-9hs7-V7ytPNdEovwORHzwSldW7nKwUHiHq4imX4mNGg1gDZ28kHiiyeoyM2GBqjYwWNoBmvbxlarWwIRmLBA6JuGCWa08wDol67F3g-miu6tARgLaExj6r7z3YJdC-HRe8JFtYYpSj5rWVn425cl_eQXn3XIW5XcKnIU1fxSOCoc7_uu_8rJ71Hh-LYVjgAKR9MpHEPe5cxJfyA9Z3-SZrqCl5h3vcb9yUWDvnbiEIlJF_aicKxOR8cdU4rFPlRrnpuP6fNA_jPcy-G_AAAA__9OSILD). Democrat Dana Van de Walker was leading Republican incumbent Audrey Young by fewer than 600 votes on Thursday.
## Suspect Charged in Deep Ellum Shooting
Federal and Dallas authorities announced Thursday that a 31-year-old man [faces seven mass-shooting charges](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAMQL8mbEFJgBSGDLew9dYbkUkMRDIEEbe0f3-iuj-41Zaf_N7PfbhDpLjN37Ci49eUhg3PTMiMxxAQdyR6rPmRd_QcN__InMJ7MMpYqbVUdgDP8YmDLoIbVeh0gU7fuqqztq5ssTjbNlNtUQU12mCsHScwCNCMwXZdq3QR3UXTWlltlKpU2TbQTKaptb-1EMwkaoUhcjpKXpDxBXmid3riUfq0FuQW5j2L6kuYXpj-PM_Sj_nSuPbC9J8TYfprJEx_WcmPllyAKJ2Im8xLShy3OcsARJDlnih6lBMGPICkX-CYMcu_EhenOFzYz0gUs72JWs0rRPq8xP8s-XTmNwAA__88doxK) from one of three Deep Ellum shootings that killed four people and wounded 15 over Halloween weekend. David Yancy turned himself in after police [released surveillance video Wednesday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupSAQhp8GO8yACFJQbGN3t93SzMJwJEExgsd7337jeYUtJ5P_y__9f76WL0w57a_fuJFr37EsO901U2t0LoHooJyvrV71IN_S7q_aSvhZJEjNheCgF_QtvWkRXXB_IVjRkRPGDlZrNehudTYSWQggLUZQxsbglYnKC6RJjmC65B6aEKCFBBign0YcoxyV8GbCICNTQCG1cvZtpUbfWGP-KW86e1-2Lru1taOy4ReTM5Pzfd_9HRGfJ5Mzni35TEzOjxiTsz_T9pyPHP_Y8YA5Y-UfNF8x53IT7byupbS0v_h1BGxPRk6GT56ACBQ3YfBcTYL4ZHTkA5DSSklvbOxOF4475ZyqNkzBa8OUP23bf478dvJfAAAA__8AB5DC) showing him pulling a handgun from his waistband. Investigators say he then fired at least 11 rounds into a crowd. He also faces a federal gun charge. Police are still hunting the gunmen who killed four people. Dallas Police Chief Daniel Comeaux urged them to come forward, saying, "_The first one who comes always gets the best deal_." The arrest comes days after U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould launched [Operation Deep Cover](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOgzAQBdDTmM5obMCBwsU2dNl2SzSxh2DJYIQncXL7FdHeYLspRv_r_Z_rdMUQw3b_xpUsv-Y0bVRyJGY6Jk-0U4yPNT_yTo7D5h6Zk39PGrSRSkkwEzoOT5pU5e0N_KAqsuoyNIMxbWOqxd4M9diD8r13sx8QqCMFQA06bRCgCvZMUwqM0gAN1H2H3ay7VrlLj17PogXygdNR80JML8xzfKcnHbVLaxXtwrxn0XwJPQo9llLqOb3a03E-CD2ep9DjyZEfj1wwxlSINpmXlDhsd_lnlHgclLk6rN9LiDFkcxEt3FcM8dPH_5zpafVvAAAA__9H2oAC), which sends more uniformed and plainclothes officers into the nightlife district. Cases brought under the program go to federal court, where those convicted are more likely to serve full sentences.

I remember the last time we saw a major market crash - it was 2008. The subprime housing lending bubble burst. Bear Stearns and Lehman Brothers went bust. The federal government had to step in with a $700 billion bailout. The S&P 500 went down 37.5% that year - if you took it from its peak in 2007 to its trough in 2009 the S&P 500, which represents the biggest blue-chip companies in the world, went down 57%. The Great Recession kicked off and lasted 18 months as unemployment shot up to double-digits.
At the time, I was 33 years old (wow!). I was like, "Okay, how does this market collapse affect me and my little education company?" Major banks were closing and layoffs were widespread. I called my company's bank - Signature Bank, which would fail 15 years later - and was reassured that our account was fine. I didn't have enough personally in savings or investment at that point to be meaningfully impacted by the crash; my little nest egg went down but it wasn't that big a deal. It was one of the bright sides of being cash poor; most of my net worth was tied up in my little company. Meanwhile, unemployed 23-year-olds were washing ashore at our company's classrooms, which specialized in preparing people to head to business school. We had to rent extra classrooms and schedule more classes because so many young workers were losing their jobs on Wall Street and were seeking shelter.
"Huh," I thought. "It's weird that while the world is falling apart, my little company is doing better than ever." We had banner years in 2008 and 2009 - it turned out that our services were somewhat more in demand in tough times than in good times. Our revenue shot up to the point where we got acquired in 2009.
The 2008 crash was the result of excessive financial chicanery - banks sliced and diced subprime loans to the point where people thought they were high-quality because the ratings agencies were asleep at the switch. Also playing a huge role - low lending standards for housing buyers who should not have been given a zero-cash down mortgage. The acronym at the time was NINJA - No Income, No Job, No Assets mortgages. Yes, that was a thing. They gave mortgages to anyone with a pulse, many of whom couldn't afford them when they reset.
That crash shook me up. You mean we had this stock market bubble because our financial institutions were morons? The growth and prosperity were illusory? And then the Feds had to bail out the banks and the bankers with taxpayer - our - money? The anger formed the Tea Party faction of the Republican Party in 2009 and then Occupy Wall Street in 2011. In my view, the anger never really ran its course, and fueled both Bernie Sanders' should-have-been-successful insurgent campaign of 2016 and Trump's "drain the swamp" rise that year.
There have been market setbacks since then with COVID and interest rates, but in my mind there hasn't been a real market crash since 2008. I feel fortunate that I lived through that one. I also lived through the crash of 2000, when the Nasdaq went from 5000 to 2000 as the Internet bubble burst. My tiny dot-com company at that time was winked out of existence, and I turned to tutoring and throwing parties to make some money in the aftermath as a 26-year old with six figures in school debt.
Now, I'm 51 years old with a family. The market started flashing crazy red signals last week; Intel lost 29% of its stock market value in a day and numerous tech stocks were in the red as they reported being cash flow negative to fund AI infrastructure. Then, just yesterday, tech stocks declined sharply. Investors are trying to figure out who is going to pay $3 trillion for the AI buildout and how. I, personally, have long been [dubious](https://substack.com/redirect/48b2078e-a234-4185-9b5e-e14cb3de7e41?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I've believed that two things could be true at the same time: AI is a game-changing technology AND the market has gotten way ahead of itself.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/97ac7d78-778c-402d-95f4-d967dd29caad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Think about the Internet circa 2000 - it did indeed change the way we live, shop and work. Amazon did eventually become a trillion-dollar company. But there was a bubble, it popped, and Pets.com, Global Crossing and dozens of other public companies were washed away as the Nasdaq shed 60% of its value. I literally attended liquidation events for dot-com companies that I'd attended launch parties for just months earlier as a hanger-on looking for free food.
AI is in the process of changing the way we think, work and love - for better or worse - and will shred [millions](https://substack.com/redirect/b39290b3-edcb-40e3-b031-025580b43ea1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of jobs. Also, these valuations and investments don't make any sense. You can't conjure up another $80 billion in revenue for Anthropic and OpenAI when companies and individuals can accomplish most tasks with cheaper open-weight models that are fine for 85% of use cases at a tiny fraction of the costs. How much are you personally spending on AI? How much is your company spending or willing to spend? Indeed, it's crystal clear that Anthropic and OpenAI's compounded growth rates are already slowing. A lot of the money that is being spent right now will never be paid back. Billions of dollars are being squandered.
One clue as to what was happening was in January 2025, when DeepSeek, a Chinese AI company, announced it could achieve comparable results to ChatGPT at a small fraction of the cost. Nvidia lost 17% immediately and the tech sector shed $590 billion in value over fears that the infrastructure buildout costs were excessive. DeepSeek was banned in many U.S. agencies due to privacy concerns. But the fear that open-weight models could do a lot of lower-order work for pennies on the dollar never actually got addressed.
I've got a newsflash for everyone but . . . most work is lower-order work.
When I was raising money for Noble Mobile, multiple investors said to me, "Andrew, if you start something with AI in the name, I'll cut you a seven-figure check right now. But I can't invest in a feel-good consumer play." Perhaps because I'm somewhat contrarian, this made me feel better about what we were doing . . . and also that numerous AI companies were going to be funded that were never going to make it. By the way, [Noble Mobile](https://substack.com/redirect/66702206-2e32-4d2f-9c2b-c83de8fdee6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is up to eight figures in annual revenue and growing and isn't going anywhere unless people decide they can do without a cellphone. I wanted to start something that would save the average consumer money and improve their outlook and mental health; I have the feeling that we'll only do better in tough times. History is repeating itself.
Much of the growth is once again illusory. Get ready for cascading loss of value at a scale that has not been seen in eighteen years. Dozens of billion-dollar companies are about to go up in smoke. The folly of some of our most exalted figures will be on full display, but hey - most of them made money on the way up.
TL;DR - When a bubble bursts, it's merciless and you don't want to be anywhere near it. Act accordingly.

Leading up to Tuesday’s elections, our movement had to stare down a national, concerted effort to prevent the American people from making their voices heard at the ballot box.
Power-hungry politicians tried to cling to power at any cost — attempting to cheat their way into unearned victories through blatant gerrymandering and voter suppression.
But with people like you fueling the fight, we held strong.
We organized against gerrymanders. We mobilized against voter suppression. We trained networks of volunteers to spread timely voter information far and wide in critical states — helping fuel incredibly strong midterm turnout.
And we proved that when we all show up, speak up, and refuse to be intimidated, we are unstoppable. **The midterm elections represented a watershed moment in our fight to protect democracy.**
**The will of the people came through in resounding numbers that can’t be ignored: flipping not only control of Congress but also the most state legislative chambers in decades. State after state, voters picked their politicians instead of the other way around. **
We’re still unpacking all the results. It honestly feels like we’re drinking from a firehose of good news—overwhelming in the best possible way.
Here are two under-the-radar victories you should savor right now:
1. The people of Missouri voted to repeal the state’s gerrymander,
2. Maryland voters approved a ballot measure that lets the state weigh in on how maps are drawn amid the national redistricting crisis.

**We’ll have more to say in the days and weeks ahead about the pro-democracy wins that you helped make possible.**
_But we know one thing for certain: the fight isn’t over. More attacks on democracy are brewing, even in just the weeks ahead._
Texas lawmakers might double down on last year’s extreme gerrymander — by trying to redraw their map again before the current governor leaves office.
And some anti-democracy lawmakers have already staked their claim on trying to skew the census, because denying a fair count is one of their best plays to deny fair maps.
**But this movement just showed that when we fight back for democracy, we can win. We can’t stop now.**

You can help power the fight to defend the census from political interference. And you can help protect the principle of free and fair elections.
**The next victories are formed in moments like this, when we choose not to rest on our laurels — but to continue the fight. And now we know what we’re truly capable of when we come together. **

| | [](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)
Dear Pro-Life Friend,

A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana.

Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her.

Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were:
_“I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.**Not now, not ever.** ”_
The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don’t count.

**That’s what abortionist “shield laws” do.** They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label!

Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m President of Students for Life of America. I’ve spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I’ve never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen.

The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back.

Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down.

**I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America.**

For years, we’ve been told abortion is now “a state issue.”

_If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,_one mailbox at a time__.

Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I’ve carried with me for most of my adult life:

_“I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?”_

I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today.

[Will you make a generous tax-deductible gift right away to help us stand with the pro-life states in this fight](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)**?**

The Solicitor General is the federal government’s lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that’s John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands.

That means the Trump Administration’s voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation.

President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. **If that’s true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government’s help protecting the laws their people passed.**

And right now, they aren’t getting enough of it.

The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills.

That’s why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what’s being shipped through the mail.

Louisiana’s attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn’t list the prescriber or a single risk.

Louisiana’s attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: _**“It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes.”**_

And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state’s pro-life laws.

Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year.

_And the women who take these deadly pills?_

A study from the _Ethics & Public Policy Center _recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. **That’s at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug’s own label!**

Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . .

Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years.

When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations.

Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation’s water and the endangered species that live in it.

And now, we’re preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We’ve also done this before and seen the impact.

On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up.
[](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb) _Roe v. Wade_ had been called “settled law” for 48 years.

Eight months later, it was gone.

I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. **But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible.**

This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand.

But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills.

[So please make your most generous tax-deductible contribution right now](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0D2u4yAQwPHT4C4WHwbigmKlyF223dKahbE9kjEIcKK9_crKexd49X80-s38ec5PoJ2O9TdEdGvKeS51fm9YkGrbMKYCezqbL_9myaW5CXHjZgbf6IXzAF1wA5jBGNOhE3ZUo-WjsN3mBoWIYbnDEqT0Vt41BGXBImpvFceO3LVQCG6EElroPnCr1aiN_rsMhmvBBo6BWir95SpYKeDRCPbep9jtbmstV6Z-MTkxOVX0Z8G-tvOaqksqOy3Yp7IyOWW4fY5gaqrFM_XAmAuTJtaVAlMPaQSXNgOT5mxx9hAz0Hpc5Qv5XdLR8GhMPS5UV1zIb9p3qsayga8R6MNrP3nmy8n_AQAA___p0YNb)**:**
**> >> $25** puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop.
**> >> $50** covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits.
**> >> $100** launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials.
**> >> $250** helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out.
**> >> $500** helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event.
Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind.
Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do.

Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her.

For Life,

Kristan Hawkins
President, _Students for Life_

P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. clean_body: And blue-state governors are protecting the abortionists who do it. |MCPREVIEWTEXT| | | | | | Dear Pro-Life Friend, A New York abortionist named Margaret Carpenter mailed chemical abortion pills to a teenage girl in Louisiana. Abortion is illegal in Louisiana, so Louisiana indicted her. Then, Louisiana asked New York to send her back to face the charges. New York Governor Kathy Hochul refused. Her exact words were: “I will not be signing an extradition order that came from the governor of Louisiana.Not now, not ever. ” The people of Louisiana passed laws to protect preborn babies and their mothers, and a governor in New York told them those laws don’t count. That’s what abortionist “shield laws” do. They protect abortionists who ship chemical abortion pills into states where abortion is illegal, and they block those states from holding anyone accountable. New York even lets the abortionist keep their name off the prescription label! Twenty-two states and Washington, D.C., have now passed shield laws like this. My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I’m President of Students for Life of America. I’ve spent 20 years fighting for preborn babies and their mothers, and I’ve never seen pro-abortion politicians this brazen. The good news is, pro-life states are fighting back. Louisiana, Alabama, and Arkansas went straight to the U.S. Supreme Court and sued New York, California, and Massachusetts to strike these shield laws down. I believe this will be the next great abortion case in America. For years, we’ve been told abortion is now “a state issue.” If the pro-abortion states win this case, that phrase means nothing. A handful of blue states will set abortion policy for the entire nation,one mailbox at a time. Before he passed away, the late Justice Antonin Scalia asked a question I’ve carried with me for most of my adult life: “I am against abortion. I want to end it! But where is the moral outcry?” I intend for Students for Life to be a key part of the solution, but I need you with me today. ? The Solicitor General is the federal government’s lawyer at the Supreme Court. Today, that’s John Sauer. When one state sues another, the Justices often ask the Solicitor General to tell them where the federal government stands. That means the Trump Administration’s voice could carry enormous weight in this case, and I intend to make sure his office hears from the Pro-Life Generation. President Trump has said again and again that abortion should be decided by the states. If that’s true, then the pro-life states deserve the federal government’s help protecting the laws their people passed. And right now, they aren’t getting enough of it. The Justice Department is still on the other side of Louisiana in its separate lawsuit against the FDA over mail-order abortion pills. That’s why the Solicitor General needs to hear from the Pro-Life Generation to make sure he understands what’s being shipped through the mail. Louisiana’s attorney general had her own office order these pills online. They got them without speaking to a doctor, and nobody verified who they were. The bottles that arrived didn’t list the prescriber or a single risk. Louisiana’s attorney general, Liz Murrill, put it plainly: “It is no different than if they were sending fentanyl in these boxes.” And the attorney general is estimating that about 800 chemical abortions are committed every month in Louisiana, despite the state’s pro-life laws. Nationwide, chemical abortion pills now account for more than two-thirds of all abortions, killing more than 600,000 preborn babies every year. And the women who take these deadly pills? A study from the Ethics & Public Policy Center recently found that nearly one in nine women suffers sepsis, infection, hemorrhaging, or another serious adverse event within 45 days of taking these pills. That’s at least 22 times the rate printed on the drug’s own label! Now picture a teenage girl in Louisiana, alone with those pills, with no doctor who will ever see her and no name on the bottle to hold accountable . . . Students for Life has been on the front lines of the fight against chemical abortion pills for years. When Louisiana sued the FDA over mailing these pills into states where abortion is illegal, my team filed a legal brief in that case alongside more than a dozen other pro-life organizations. Then, we put the FDA on notice for ignoring what chemical abortion pill waste is doing to our nation’s water and the endangered species that live in it. And now, we’re preparing to file a legal brief in this shield law case, too. We’ve also done this before and seen the impact. On the opening day of the Supreme Court’s term in October 2021, we carried more than half a million signed Moral Outcry Petitions up the marble steps of the Court. They were printed on two scrolls, each one 160 feet long, and it took a human chain of pro-lifers just to hold them up. Roe v. Wade had been called “settled law” for 48 years. Eight months later, it was gone. I won’t tell you those scrolls ended Roe by themselves. But I will tell you that pro-lifers who refuse to stay quiet have a way of changing what everyone else thinks is possible. This time, our team will be back on those steps with a legal brief in hand. But I can’t get there on good intentions. Legal work costs money, and so does every campus stop where we tell students the TRUTH about these deadly pills. : >> $25 puts pro-life materials in the hands of students at one campus stop. >> $50 covers a tank of gas for a day of campus visits. >> $100 launches a brand-new Students for Life group with flyers, postcards, and materials. >> $250 helps put our team on a campus that has tried to keep us out. >> $500 helps cover the security costs we now face at a single event. Every dollar you give helps us expose chemical abortion pills, reach more students with the TRUTH, and keep fighting for every mother and baby these shield laws leave behind. Governor Hochul defiantly said “not now, not ever.” I’d like to answer her with a legal brief at the Supreme Court, and I’d like you standing with me when we do. Thank you for standing with me, and with every preborn baby in a state that chose to protect her. For Life, Kristan Hawkins President, Students for Life P.S. – Three pro-life states just asked the Supreme Court to strike down the shield laws protecting abortionists who mail chemical abortion pills across state lines. The federal government’s voice could make all the difference. subject: He survived 9/11. Now he may die in prison.
body:
My brother defended himself... now he’s charged with murder

View in Web Browser
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.com/click/e2861310/UaHR0cHM6Ly9vZGIubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvS2Zidms2Wk1Ubg/SZW1haWxfZnJlZXRoaW5rZXJkYWlseV9jb20yNjExMDY/LbmNscExQdWRMZQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNiZ0F1M3o0VThkZ29sc10/gau3UZw/s4r4d348f43

Dear Patriot,
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Never in a million years did I think I would be writing an email like
this.

BUT THE TRUTH IS, MY FAMILY AND I ARE OUT OF OPTIONS. AND YOU'RE OUR
ONLY HOPE.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

[Image showing officer, police officer, and captain]
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

This is a photo of my brother, Anthony DeLustro.

Anthony spent more than 20 years serving citizens as an NYPD cop,
hunting down dangerous drug dealers and busting up drug dens.

On 9/11, he helped evacuate hundreds of people from one of the
buildings just before it collapsed. Since that day, he's been battling
cancer and Ground Zero Lung from the toxic fumes.

We really thought Anthony had been through the worst of it.

THEN HE TOOK A POLICE JOB IN A SMALL SOUTH CAROLINA TOWN SO HE COULD
SPEND HIS GOLDEN YEARS CLOSE TO HIS GRANDKIDS.

How could I have known he was about to face the greatest danger of his
life?

I'm not talking about a drug dealer or a terrorist or even cancer...

...BUT A LOCAL PROSECUTOR HELLBENT ON DESTROYING MY BROTHER FOR
DEFENDING HIMSELF WHEN HE WAS THE VICTIM OF A ROAD RAGE INCIDENT.

Let me explain.

The day Anthony was attacked, he was off duty. He and his wife had
stopped for lunch after spending the morning at a "Coffee With A Cop"
community event.

As they tried to pull out of the crowded restaurant parking lot,
another driver jumped out of his car and began screaming threats at my
brother.

ANTHONY TRIED TO CALM HIM DOWN.

BUT THE MAN ATTACKED HIM, STRIKING HIM OVER AND OVER.

Anthony pulled out his badge and told the man he was under arrest.

Instead of complying, the man knocked the badge out of Anthony's hand,
got in his car, and tried to flee...

...dragging my brother with his vehicle and running over his legs.

In that moment, Anthony knew he was about to be crushed to death in
front of his own wife.

So he fired a single shot into his attacker's arm, bringing the car to
a stop.

Anthony's quick thinking saved his life.

But the road rage driver who attacked him died at the scene.

When I got the call that Anthony had been assaulted and was in the
hospital with serious injuries, I was so relieved he was alive.

BUT MY RELIEF TURNED INTO SHOCK WHEN MY BROTHER WAS ARRESTED AND
CHARGED WITH MURDER.

He hadn't even recovered from his injuries when the local prosecutor
dragged him in front of a judge and had him locked up in jail.

And now he's facing up to 30 YEARS in prison.

Anthony is 64 years old.

If he's convicted...

...HE'LL LIKELY SPEND THE REST OF HIS LIFE LOCKED UP - AND DIE IN
PRISON - FOR DEFENDING HIMSELF.

THAT'S WHY I'M WRITING YOU - SOMEONE I'VE NEVER MET - TO ASK YOU TO
HELP MY BROTHER.
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

Anthony doesn't deserve this.

He served as a cop for four decades and never once faced discipline.
He has a spotless record full of awards and commendations.

Several years ago, Anthony and his wife took their two granddaughters
into their home. They've been raising them ever since.

You can imagine the pain it's caused these poor girls to have their
grandfather locked up and treated like a common criminal.

We were almost out of hope.

And then we found out about the LAW ENFORCEMENT LEGAL DEFENSE FUND.

LELDF is a national group that's helped dozens of innocent officers
clear their names when they're wrongly accused by radical prosecutors.

And they've agreed to help Anthony too.

Not only are they getting my brother the legal defense he deserves -
they're also raising money to pay for the best attorneys and expert
witnesses available.

Which brings me to the reason I wrote you today:

WILL YOU HELP MY BROTHER FIGHT THESE UNJUST CHARGES BY DONATING TO THE
LELDF?
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

The legal bills are already overwhelming. And we haven't even gotten
to trial.

Anthony and his wife have already drained almost their entire life's
savings fighting to free him.

So any amount you can give today will help.

And because LELDF is a non-profit organization, your gift is
completely tax-deductible.

WHATEVER YOU CAN AFFORD TO GIVE, I'M ASKING YOU TO PLEASE MAKE YOUR
GIFT TODAY.

After four decades serving his community, the cancer, and the injuries
from his attack, Anthony deserves to spend his retirement years in
peace with his family - NOT locked up behind bars for the rest of his
life.

But that's exactly what will happen unless patriots like you step up
on his behalf.

Thank you for taking the time to read my email today.

THANK YOU IN ADVANCE FOR MAKING YOUR TAX-DEDUCTIBLE GIFT TO HELP
ANTHONY FIGHT TO CLEAR HIS NAME.

And please, keep my brother in your prayers.

_FRANK DELUSTRO_

P.S. Anthony didn’t know it at the time, but the road-rage maniac
who attacked him had a criminal record. Maybe that’s why he was so
eager to flee the scene after my brother arrested him.

PLEASE HELP SAVE ANTHONY FROM SPENDING THE REST OF HIS LIFE BEHIND
BARS. MAKE A TAX-DEDUCTIBLE GIFT OF ANY AMOUNT TO THE LAW ENFORCEMENT
LEGAL DEFENSE FUND RIGHT AWAY.

STAND WITH OFFICER DELUSTRO
[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

[https://link.email.freethinkerdaily.

_More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates
unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue.
The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank
them for their service. To read more about our mission or the other
Law Enforcement officers we're defending, please visit www.leldf.org.
And remember - Blue Lives Matter!_

November 6, 2026

In a massacre that would embarrass Genghis Khan, the Democrats obliterated Republicans in the midterm elections. At the time of this writing, the Democrats have picked up seven Senate seats giving them a total of 54. Two races, Alaska and Mississippi, are too close to call, but odds are they will both go Democratic. In the House the Democrats have already won thirty seats and political pundits believe this number could climb to 46. Thus, the Democrats will have about 260 to 175 majority.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a089325-29fb-4fa1-8f44-99ce5ec50cd3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

Traditional Republican states such as South Carolina, Ohio, Kansas and Iowa elected Democratic senators. And the liberal wish of turning Texas Blue finally came true, as the incumbent Republican Governor was vanquished and the open Senate seat was won by Democrat James Talerico by 12%. The State House also flipped to the Democrats as did all the constitutional offices.

In my home state of Connecticut, elected Republicans in our Assembly and Senate are rarer than Ivory-Billed Woodpeckers. Eight Senate seats were lost and now the Democrats have a 33-3 majority! The Governor, the Senators, constitutional officers and the Congressmen are all Democrats.

How did this happen?
**The invasion of Iran was a disaster.** With neither the consent of Congress nor the American people, President Trump decided he was going to bring peace to the Middle East by neutering Iran. But he had no plan. Only regime change is going to change Iran's policies, and this is not possible without an armed insurgency by Iranians, American ground troops or the use of nuclear weapons. The result, the clever Iranians looked at American polls, blocked the Strait of Hormuz and caused gas and diesel prices to skyrocket. Hello Democrats.

**People are tired of President Trump 's antics**. The inflationary tariffs were bad enough, but having his family promote cryptocurrency scams while his son-in-law Jared Kushner is extorting foreign leaders to[ invest in his hedge fund](https://substack.com/redirect/5087973e-a891-4d5c-9290-38c5e5a82aed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is a bit much. And why insult Canada by saying it should become our 51st state while imposing lumber tariffs that increased housing costs. And sucking up to the barbarian Putin has accomplished nothing. The federal deficit is higher than ever. So much for fiscal conservatism.
**President Trump has lost his juice**. The conventional wisdom was that either Vance or Rubio would be the presidential nominee and if Trump choose one of them, the other would bow out. This has been thrown out the window. It may well be that both Vance and Rubio are too tainted by Trump and Republicans will look at more electable candidates such as Ron DeSantis or Nikki Haley.

**Trump was not the only issue**. [70% of the American people](https://substack.com/redirect/f4d8d130-6a9f-43fc-b345-7448514ce907?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) believe America is on the wrong tract. This number is consistent no matter what party is in the White House. We once had a country in which a man could support a family on one income. Now you can barely do it on two incomes. Young people are refusing to marry because they can't afford to. Neither party has any concrete solutions to high housing, health insurance and car prices. Taxes are too high but cutting them is politically impossible, especially with our massive $40 trillion deficit.

**This Blue Wave makes it easier for Republicans to win the White House in 2028.** Americans love divided government since it prevents the extremes of either party from imposing their will. The Democrats have relatively large majorities in the House and Senate, and many voters do not want to see an unchecked Democratic president, especially if the Democrats nominate a socialist such as Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (AOC).

**Israel will have to fight harder for its existence.** Even prominent Jewish politicians such as Bernie Saunders and Jamie Raskin have embraced the Palestinian cause, and Democratic rallies are replete with Palestinian flags. The swing state of Michigan just elected a Democratic Senator, Abdul El-Sayed, who is openly hostile to Israel's existence. Unless President Trump by some miracle can turn the war around with Iran, Israel may soon find itself abandoned by the American political class.
But as bad as this election was for Republicans, it is not without precedent. The Democrats lost 63 seats during the Clinton presidency in 1994 and 54 seats during the Obama presidency in 2010 - more than the Republicans lost this cycle. Yet both Clinton and Obama won reelection easily. And there is no better street fight than Donald Trump, even when he is a lame duck. It would be foolish to count him out.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8ad38c65-0ab6-4436-bfe5-a4a77d71f149?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

But if this election shows anything, America is an unhappy country in spite of our affluence. People find happiness in faith, family, friends and financial security. The pollical, economic and cultural changes of the past two generations have made this possible for fewer people.
