# Iran
* **Trump threatens to "destroy what is left" of Iran, says decision on new strikes coming soon: **President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he would soon decide whether to launch another round of U.S. strikes on Iran, threatening to "destroy what is left of the country."
* Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said that the U.S. must decide whether to "go further" to prevent Iran from rebuilding its military and nuclear capabilities, claiming that the country will already need "25 years" to recover from the destruction the U.S. and Israel inflicted on it. "I would prefer not to destroy what is left of the country, if possible, but I may have to do so. You will know very soon," he said.
* Trump also said that after more than eight months of war, the U.S. controls "everything that we've wanted to control" in Iran, and that Tehran cannot take action on its nuclear program "without approval."
* **Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in Strait of Hormuz:** Two oil tankers caught fire and were immobilized after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Both vessels had switched off their navigation and identification systems, the IRGC claimed, and were attempting to exit the strait through a prohibited passage, with U.S. military support.
* The IRGC said that the strait would "remain closed" until the U.S. meets Iran's seven conditions for a peace deal, adding that attempts by the U.S. military Central Command to force tankers through mined, unauthorized routes would result in "successive defeats."
* Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) reported an explosion aboard a tanker transiting the strait, approximately 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman, at 1 a.m. local time Friday. It was unclear whether the incident involved either tanker reported by Iran. UKMTO said the vessel continued its voyage, with all crew members accounted for.

# Palestine
* **Two Palestinians die from wounds sustained in Israeli airstrikes on Gaza:** A female medical student at the Islamic University of Gaza [died](https://substack.com/redirect/60c464d4-3edc-4a7c-8c6a-245ae77554e4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Friday from injuries sustained in an Israeli strike on the university about a week ago, WAFA reported. A man died from wounds sustained in an Israeli attack on the Al-Shati refugee camp several days earlier.
* **94% of Gaza 's population needs shelter assistance, UN says: **1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza, or 94% of the population, need shelter assistance as winter approaches, with 270 displaced families living in four UN shelters at very high risk of collapse, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/476f836c-af46-42f3-8fa6-65014ef49663?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a new report from the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East, known as UNRWA. Meanwhile, 84% of Gaza's population faces frequent disruptions to clean water supplies, while 89% of households lack basic hygiene items.
* Israeli restrictions have prevented UNRWA from directly bringing aid into Gaza since March 2025, leaving food and shelter supplies for hundreds of thousands of Palestinians stranded outside the territory.
* Read Drop Site News contributor Abdel Qadder Sabbah's [latest report](https://substack.com/redirect/f2baafb0-055e-4fe6-89da-d764c55d199b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Gaza: Displaced Palestinians are living in tents, without proper shelter, as winter approaches.
* **Israel destroys 100,000 olive trees this year in the occupied West Bank; Gaza faces "ecocide": **Israeli forces and settlers [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/ad04b3e9-43cd-4226-906e-8818fb56ad95?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 760 environmental attacks across the West Bank in the first nine months of 2026, destroying approximately 100,000 olive trees and causing an estimated $67 million in losses, according to the Palestinian Environmental Quality Authority. The attacks targeted farmland, water sources, irrigation networks, and natural reserves, while Israeli forces and settlers also dumped hazardous waste and demolished infrastructure.
* In Gaza, the authority said Israeli attacks have left up to 68 million tons of rubble, including four million tons of hazardous waste, and destroyed 82% of agricultural land, 97% of fruit and olive trees, and 84% of water and sanitation infrastructure. The authority described the destruction as "ecocide."
* **Israeli forces arrest 17 during olive harvest as settlers attack Palestinians across West Bank:**
* **Ramallah:** Israeli forces [detained](https://substack.com/redirect/b7a70625-e690-4e60-8d72-6a527b1d2d58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 17 people, including 12 international solidarity activists, two foreign journalists, and three Palestinians, after settlers attacked farmers and volunteers harvesting olives in Kafr Ni'ma on Friday, according to WAFA.
* **Nablus:** Settlers [stole](https://substack.com/redirect/1045029b-0777-4bf5-bfc6-82872ff93f60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olives from a farm in Al-Masoudiya, cut electricity poles supplying a home housing three families in Burin, and set fire to residential tents in Duma.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/25ed39e2-33ab-430e-ac06-762f46e04b94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian man in Yatta after he and his son confronted settlers who had released livestock onto Palestinian farmland. In Hebron city, Israeli forces raided homes in Jabal Jawhar and Jabal al-Rahma, converting one into a military post, and fired tear gas at residents and traders attending a weekly livestock market.
* **Occupied East Jerusalem:** Israeli authorities [forced](https://substack.com/redirect/1d8902a4-b442-4ef6-8b16-80461e6fc8fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two Palestinian families to demolish their own homes in Jabal Mukabber, displacing 18 people. The two homes, each measuring approximately 50 square meters, were built in 2020.
* **Netanyahu calls Trump 's decision to end U.S. military aid a shift toward "partnership": **Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office portrayed President Donald Trump's decision to end U.S. military aid to Israel at the end of this year as a transition from aid to partnership, claiming the move demonstrates the "strength and sophistication" of U.S.-Israel relations. In a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/727a0d5a-3a51-42c9-b0dc-d43ad292f445?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, Netanyahu's office said that Israel had used decades of American military assistance "both to defend itself and to confront enemies who threaten America and the West," describing the funding as a longstanding bipartisan commitment.
* Netanyahu's spokesperson Doron Spielman told Fox News that the Israeli leader had been working with Trump to replace aid with "partnership and mutual investment."

# Yemen
* **Yemen 's Saudi-backed government claims 440 Ansarallah fighters killed or wounded; strikes on Taiz market cause over 30 casualties: **Yemen's Saudi-backed forces claimed they "neutralized" 440 Ansarallah fighters and destroyed or disabled 132 military vehicles and heavy weapons in nearly 1,300 attacks since launching Operation Dawn of Yemen on October 5.
* Meanwhile, Saudi-coalition airstrikes hit a market three times in al-Wazi'iyah, Taiz governorate, on Friday morning, Ansarallah-run Al Masirah TV reported. The attacks killed or wounded more than 30 people, with rescue teams still searching for missing victims.
* **Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Ansarallah attacks over Saudi Arabia:** The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Ansarallah toward Najran in southwestern Saudi Arabia, as well as a drone over the Mecca region, the coalition said on Friday.
* **Turkish parliament approves trilateral defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan:** Turkey's parliament [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/ce1d29c8-618f-41f6-b91f-237087cc31d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 279-119 on Thursday to ratify the "Mecca Agreement on Joint Defense" with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, clearing the way for the trilateral security pact, signed in August, to take effect. The agreement aims to strengthen collective security and expand military cooperation among the three countries. During Turkey's parliamentary debate, ruling Justice and Development Party lawmaker Ziya Altunyaldiz said that the pact was not directed against any third country and was intended to prevent further conflicts, not produce them.

* **Sen. Chuck Grassley denies rumor of resignation during the lame-duck session:** Sen. **Chuck Grassley** [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/96abf6e0-29d7-4abf-ad20-153e3984a902?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) rumors that he would resign before the new Congress is sworn. The DOJ has sought to intervene in the election, citing voter confusion over the addition of Daniel J. Sullivan to the ballot.
* **In the Mississippi Senate race, Scott Colom widens lead by 1,800+ votes:** Democratic candidate **Scott Colom** [widened](https://substack.com/redirect/cad36d22-a3b1-48cf-ad5b-0d37f3e5d722?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his lead over Sen. **Cindy Hyde-Smith** in Mississippi's Senate race to more than 1,800 votes on Thursday, according to Decision Desk HQ. Earlier in the week, Colom was in a virtual dead heat with Hyde-Smith, at one point leading the incumbent by just 28 votes. Mississippi is awaiting 3,600 outstanding mail ballots.
* **Aggressive DOJ civil rights director Harmeet Dhillon resigns: Harmeet Dhillon** resigned as head of the DOJ civil rights division, Attorney General **Todd Blanche** announced on Thursday. In her official capacity, Dhillon aggressively attacked left-wing groups, universities, and state election apparatuses. She ran the DOJ's largest ever election-monitoring operation, which did not produce a single announced finding of voter fraud. She [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/90391a1d-0969-4535-b01b-21bdb2814bdf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) intends to return to the law firm she founded, Dhillon Law Group.
* **Calif. Gov. Gavin Newsom commutes sentences of all 548 death-row inmates, rejecting "state-sanctioned killing": **California Gov. **Gavin Newsom**[reduced](https://substack.com/redirect/31cb1350-faea-47ff-adb9-c3dee9f8bd85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the death sentences of every prisoner in the state to life without parole on Thursday. "State-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values," he said. With the sweep of his pen, Newsom cancelled about 25% of the nation's current death sentences. The incoming Gov.-elect **Xavier Becerra** has pledged to maintain a moratorium on executions that Newsom signed earlier in his term.
* **Bloomberg: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly considering exit from Trump administration:** Secretary of State **Marco Rubio** is weighing a possible departure from the Trump administration, Bloomberg [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/d83039cf-2b52-4912-ad5e-3ec76446f3d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The White House reportedly asked him to remain in the role. Rubio dismissed the Bloomberg report, telling the New York Times that it has "always been my plan" to stay until Trump's second term ends.

# Other International News
* **Paraguayan president Santiago Pe ña resigns, following collapse of Ueno bank and alleged corruption:** On Thursday, President of Paraguay Santiago Peña [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/50895272-5ec3-4724-b848-631cd891bcc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his resignation from the presidency. He said, in a recorded address, that he was stepping down with "the stability of our country, social peace, and the need to preserve our democratic institutions in mind." His resignation comes amid the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, which has left nearly half of Paraguayans unable to access their accounts. Minutes after resigning, he was impeached in a unanimous vote in the lower house of parliament. Lawmakers accused Peña of corruption, which he denies. Until March 2025, he was a shareholder of Ueno's parent company, Grupo Vazquez. The collapse of Ueno has already led to the resignation of the head of the Central Bank; led to the detention of eight Ueno bank executives; and sent Paraguay's sovereign-bond price tumbling. Ueno administered almost $850 million in public funds.
* **U.S. imposes new sanctions on Cuba:** Secretary of State Marco Rubio [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/c73e3743-b4af-4d59-a945-560f15464998?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new sanctions on Cuban industries on Thursday, targeting its "crude oil shipping network," state-owned entities, and "China-based suppliers of Cuba's military forces." Rubio accused Cuban military officials and "regime insiders" of profiting from "opaque offshore networks" and reiterated an unsubstantiated allegation that the island serves as "a staging ground for a global coalition of hostile anti-American actors." The Trump administration has repeatedly imposed sanctions on the island's industries and its political leaders, and it has maintained its suffocating blockade of fuel to the country.
* **Russia launches attacks on Ukraine 's energy infrastructure; death toll from earlier attack on Ukrainian aid center rises to 50+: **Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure [caused](https://substack.com/redirect/c923167c-a9fe-4630-b8cf-d28d12866bf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) new power outages in seven regions, Reuters reported. Strikes late Thursday and early Friday hit Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kyiv, Kharkiv, and Chernihiv.
* Separately on Friday, the death toll from a Monday attack on an aid center in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia [rose](https://substack.com/redirect/638ca360-38af-4d24-b557-ca5cad249f42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to 53, according to Ukraine's emergency service. Local police said earlier this week that as many as 39 people could still be trapped under the rubble.
* **Indonesian police accuse a fourth official in alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto:** In an investigation into the wiretapping of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, police [named](https://substack.com/redirect/038e3c73-5128-4885-bb89-d857f979b10e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a fourth suspect on Friday, who they referred to by his initials, SU. Local media identified the suspect as Slamet Uliandi, who led the Criminal Investigation Agency's information and technology unit from 2021 to 2026. Earlier this week, police arrested three senior officers in connection with the wiretapping case, including Prabowo's chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo.
* **Macau pro-democracy activist sentenced to 12 years in prison:** A court in Macau, a special administrative region of China, [sentenced](https://substack.com/redirect/54f90931-1b57-4045-92ef-d7ec7e7cf789?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the pro-democracy activist and former lawmaker Au Kam-san to 12-and-a-half years in prison on Friday. After a national-security trial that was held behind closed doors, Au, 69, was found guilty of "subverting state power by spreading false information" during Macau's leadership elections in 2024. The court said that he worked with "hostile organizations" abroad and leaked confidential information to overseas groups. Human Rights Watch condemned the sentence, and urged the European Union and Portugal, which formerly controlled Macau, to push for Au's release.
* **Tanzania sentences opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in prison:** On Friday, a three-judge panel in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/5640ad25-5e4a-424e-820e-4d858ea78c8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against Tundu Lissu, leader of the political opposition, convicting him of incitement for statements he made before the 2025 elections. The panel dropped a treason charge that carried a possible punishment of death. Lissu, the leader of the Chadema Party, called the trial "political persecution," and accused the judges of coordinating with the government. "I was not charged with incitement but you judges are convicting me with it just to impress the person who gives you the titles," he told the court. "I believe these were directives." He was arrested before the elections of October 2025, which the ruling President Samia Suluhu Hassan went on to win with 98% of the vote. His near-total victory prompted mass protests, which the government subdued by killing thousands of people, according to the political opposition and human-rights groups. British and EU lawmakers said that the case against Lissu was politically motivated and demanded his release.
* **Egyptian soldiers killed in operation on Sudan border:** Two Egyptian army officers were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/7edfff49-e4e5-467f-b2b8-1bfa07521302?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during a military crackdown on illegal gold mining along the border with Sudan, Reuters reported. One of the dead was a high-ranking officer. The Egyptian military began its campaign against illegal gold mining in June.

Photo by Daniel Duarte / AFP via Getty Images. Friday, November 6, 2026 -** Iran: President Donald Trump threatens to "destroy what is left" of Iran, says decision on new strikes coming soon. Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in Strait of Hormuz. Palestine: Two Palestinians die from wounds sustained in Israeli airstrikes on Gaza. 94% of Gaza's population needs shelter assistance, UN says. Israel destroys 100,000 olive trees this year in the occupied West Bank; Gaza faces "ecocide." Israeli forces arrest 17 during olive harvest as settlers attack Palestinians across occupied West Bank. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu calls Trump's decision to end U.S. military aid a shift toward "partnership." Yemen: Yemen's Saudi-backed government claims 440 Ansarallah fighters killed or wounded; strikes on Taiz market cause over 30 casualties. Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Ansarallah attacks over Saudi Arabia. Turkish parliament approves trilateral defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan. Lebanon: Israeli forces fire on olive-pickers, detain resident amid new ceasefire violations in southern Lebanon. U.S.: Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed backs Chris Van Hollen over Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader. Sen. Chuck Grassley denies rumors of resignation during lame-duck session. Trump says votes for Alaska's "Fake Dan Sullivan" should go to Sen. Dan Sullivan. Democrat Scott Colom widens lead in Mississippi Senate race by over 1,800 votes. DOJ civil rights chief Harmeet Dhillon resigns. California Gov. Gavin Newsom commutes death sentences of all 548 death-row inmates. Bloomberg: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly considering leaving Trump administration. International: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigns amid bank collapse and corruption allegations. U.S. imposes new sanctions on Cuba. Russian strikes cause power outages across seven Ukrainian regions; death toll from aid center attack rises to 53. Indonesian police name fourth suspect in alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto. Macau pro-democracy activist sentenced to 12.5 years in prison. Tanzania sentences opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in prison. Two Egyptian army officers killed in operation along Sudan border. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Trump threatens to "destroy what is left" of Iran, says decision on new strikes coming soon: President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he would soon decide whether to launch another round of U.S. strikes on Iran, threatening to "destroy what is left of the country." Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump said that the U.S. must decide whether to "go further" to prevent Iran from rebuilding its military and nuclear capabilities, claiming that the country will already need "25 years" to recover from the destruction the U.S. and Israel inflicted on it. "I would prefer not to destroy what is left of the country, if possible, but I may have to do so. You will know very soon," he said. Trump also said that after more than eight months of war, the U.S. controls "everything that we've wanted to control" in Iran, and that Tehran cannot take action on its nuclear program "without approval." Iran says two oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in Strait of Hormuz: Two oil tankers caught fire and were immobilized after striking naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). Both vessels had switched off their navigation and identification systems, the IRGC claimed, and were attempting to exit the strait through a prohibited passage, with U.S. military support. The IRGC said that the strait would "remain closed" until the U.S. meets Iran's seven conditions for a peace deal, adding that attempts by the U.S. military Central Command to force tankers through mined, unauthorized routes would result in "successive defeats." Separately, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) reported an explosion aboard a tanker transiting the strait, approximately 16 nautical miles east of Khasab, Oman, at 1 a.m. local time Friday. It was unclear whether the incident involved either tanker reported by Iran. UKMTO said the vessel continued its voyage, with all crew members accounted for. Palestine Two Palestinians die from wounds sustained in Israeli airstrikes on Gaza: A female medical student at the Islamic University of Gaza on Friday from injuries sustained in an Israeli strike on the university about a week ago, WAFA reported. A man died from wounds sustained in an Israeli attack on the Al-Shati refugee camp several days earlier. 94% of Gaza 's population needs shelter assistance, UN says: 1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza, or 94% of the population, need shelter assistance as winter approaches, with 270 displaced families living in four UN shelters at very high risk of collapse, to a new report from the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East, known as UNRWA. Meanwhile, 84% of Gaza's population faces frequent disruptions to clean water supplies, while 89% of households lack basic hygiene items. Israeli restrictions have prevented UNRWA from directly bringing aid into Gaza since March 2025, leaving food and shelter supplies for hundreds of thousands of Palestinians stranded outside the territory. Read Drop Site News contributor Abdel Qadder Sabbah's from Gaza: Displaced Palestinians are living in tents, without proper shelter, as winter approaches. Israel destroys 100,000 olive trees this year in the occupied West Bank; Gaza faces "ecocide": Israeli forces and settlers 760 environmental attacks across the West Bank in the first nine months of 2026, destroying approximately 100,000 olive trees and causing an estimated $67 million in losses, according to the Palestinian Environmental Quality Authority. The attacks targeted farmland, water sources, irrigation networks, and natural reserves, while Israeli forces and settlers also dumped hazardous waste and demolished infrastructure. In Gaza, the authority said Israeli attacks have left up to 68 million tons of rubble, including four million tons of hazardous waste, and destroyed 82% of agricultural land, 97% of fruit and olive trees, and 84% of water and sanitation infrastructure. The authority described the destruction as "ecocide." Israeli forces arrest 17 during olive harvest as settlers attack Palestinians across West Bank: Ramallah: Israeli forces 17 people, including 12 international solidarity activists, two foreign journalists, and three Palestinians, after settlers attacked farmers and volunteers harvesting olives in Kafr Ni'ma on Friday, according to WAFA. Nablus: Settlers olives from a farm in Al-Masoudiya, cut electricity poles supplying a home housing three families in Burin, and set fire to residential tents in Duma. Hebron: Israeli forces a Palestinian man in Yatta after he and his son confronted settlers who had released livestock onto Palestinian farmland. In Hebron city, Israeli forces raided homes in Jabal Jawhar and Jabal al-Rahma, converting one into a military post, and fired tear gas at residents and traders attending a weekly livestock market. Occupied East Jerusalem: Israeli authorities two Palestinian families to demolish their own homes in Jabal Mukabber, displacing 18 people. The two homes, each measuring approximately 50 square meters, were built in 2020. Netanyahu calls Trump 's decision to end U.S. military aid a shift toward "partnership": Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office portrayed President Donald Trump's decision to end U.S. military aid to Israel at the end of this year as a transition from aid to partnership, claiming the move demonstrates the "strength and sophistication" of U.S.-Israel relations. In a on X, Netanyahu's office said that Israel had used decades of American military assistance "both to defend itself and to confront enemies who threaten America and the West," describing the funding as a longstanding bipartisan commitment. Netanyahu's spokesperson Doron Spielman told Fox News that the Israeli leader had been working with Trump to replace aid with "partnership and mutual investment." Yemen Yemen 's Saudi-backed government claims 440 Ansarallah fighters killed or wounded; strikes on Taiz market cause over 30 casualties: Yemen's Saudi-backed forces claimed they "neutralized" 440 Ansarallah fighters and destroyed or disabled 132 military vehicles and heavy weapons in nearly 1,300 attacks since launching Operation Dawn of Yemen on October 5. Meanwhile, Saudi-coalition airstrikes hit a market three times in al-Wazi'iyah, Taiz governorate, on Friday morning, Ansarallah-run Al Masirah TV reported. The attacks killed or wounded more than 30 people, with rescue teams still searching for missing victims. Saudi-led coalition intercepts two Ansarallah attacks over Saudi Arabia: The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by Ansarallah toward Najran in southwestern Saudi Arabia, as well as a drone over the Mecca region, the coalition said on Friday. Turkish parliament approves trilateral defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan: Turkey's parliament 279-119 on Thursday to ratify the "Mecca Agreement on Joint Defense" with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, clearing the way for the trilateral security pact, signed in August, to take effect. The agreement aims to strengthen collective security and expand military cooperation among the three countries. During Turkey's parliamentary debate, ruling Justice and Development Party lawmaker Ziya Altunyaldiz said that the pact was not directed against any third country and was intended to prevent further conflicts, not produce them. Lebanon Israeli forces fire on olive-pickers, detain resident amid new ceasefire violations in southern Lebanon: Marjeyoun: Israeli forces from Kfar Kila toward the outskirts of Deir Mimas, firing near residents harvesting olives and forcing them to flee. The troops blocked entry and exit from the village and detained a resident, taking him to an unknown location. Bint Jbeil: Israeli forces carried out a massive explosion on the outskirts of Beit Yahoun, toward Konin. Nabatieh: Israeli forces the outskirts of Mifdoun. U.S. News Michigan Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed backs Chris Van Hollen over Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader: In an interview with CNN on Thursday, Abdul El-Sayed he supports Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader. El-Sayed said he would look at other options if Van Hollen did not run for the position, adding that he will support a leader who intends to pass legislation. Newly elected Democratic senators in Kansas, Illinois, and Maine--Adam Hamilton , Juliana Stratton , and Troy Jackson --have said they will not back Sen. Chuck Schumer for the post. Sen. Chuck Grassley denies rumor of resignation during the lame-duck session: Sen. Chuck Grassley rumors that he would resign before the new Congress is sworn. If Grassley remains in office, he would prevent the incoming Democratic Gov. Rob Sand from appointing a successor. Grassley's chief of staff said on Thursday that the 93-year-old Iowa Republican "remains committed to delivering for the people of Iowa, who overwhelmingly elected him to a six-year term in 2022." Grassley has not said whether he will seek a ninth term in 2028. Trump says votes cast for Alaska 's "Fake Dan Sullivan" should go to Sen. Dan Sullivan: President Trump on Thursday that the votes cast for Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. "should be immediately given to the REAL Dan Sullivan." As of Friday morning, 75% of the votes were counted, and Democratic candidate Mary Peltola maintains a close lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan. The DOJ has sought to intervene in the election, citing voter confusion over the addition of Daniel J. Sullivan to the ballot. In the Mississippi Senate race, Scott Colom widens lead by 1,800+ votes: Democratic candidate Scott Colom his lead over Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi's Senate race to more than 1,800 votes on Thursday, according to Decision Desk HQ. Earlier in the week, Colom was in a virtual dead heat with Hyde-Smith, at one point leading the incumbent by just 28 votes. Mississippi is awaiting 3,600 outstanding mail ballots. Aggressive DOJ civil rights director Harmeet Dhillon resigns: Harmeet Dhillon resigned as head of the DOJ civil rights division, Attorney General Todd Blanche announced on Thursday. In her official capacity, Dhillon aggressively attacked left-wing groups, universities, and state election apparatuses. She ran the DOJ's largest ever election-monitoring operation, which did not produce a single announced finding of voter fraud. She intends to return to the law firm she founded, Dhillon Law Group. Calif. Gov. Gavin Newsom commutes sentences of all 548 death-row inmates, rejecting "state-sanctioned killing": California Gov. Gavin Newsom the death sentences of every prisoner in the state to life without parole on Thursday. "State-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California's values," he said. With the sweep of his pen, Newsom cancelled about 25% of the nation's current death sentences. The incoming Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra has pledged to maintain a moratorium on executions that Newsom signed earlier in his term. Bloomberg: Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly considering exit from Trump administration: Secretary of State Marco Rubio is weighing a possible departure from the Trump administration, Bloomberg . The White House reportedly asked him to remain in the role. Rubio dismissed the Bloomberg report, telling the New York Times that it has "always been my plan" to stay until Trump's second term ends. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Paraguayan president Santiago Pe ña resigns, following collapse of Ueno bank and alleged corruption: On Thursday, President of Paraguay Santiago Peña his resignation from the presidency. He said, in a recorded address, that he was stepping down with "the stability of our country, social peace, and the need to preserve our democratic institutions in mind." His resignation comes amid the collapse of the digital bank Ueno, which has left nearly half of Paraguayans unable to access their accounts. Minutes after resigning, he was impeached in a unanimous vote in the lower house of parliament. Lawmakers accused Peña of corruption, which he denies. Until March 2025, he was a shareholder of Ueno's parent company, Grupo Vazquez. The collapse of Ueno has already led to the resignation of the head of the Central Bank; led to the detention of eight Ueno bank executives; and sent Paraguay's sovereign-bond price tumbling. Ueno administered almost $850 million in public funds. U.S. imposes new sanctions on Cuba: Secretary of State Marco Rubio new sanctions on Cuban industries on Thursday, targeting its "crude oil shipping network," state-owned entities, and "China-based suppliers of Cuba's military forces." Rubio accused Cuban military officials and "regime insiders" of profiting from "opaque offshore networks" and reiterated an unsubstantiated allegation that the island serves as "a staging ground for a global coalition of hostile anti-American actors." The Trump administration has repeatedly imposed sanctions on the island's industries and its political leaders, and it has maintained its suffocating blockade of fuel to the country. Russia launches attacks on Ukraine 's energy infrastructure; death toll from earlier attack on Ukrainian aid center rises to 50+: Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure new power outages in seven regions, Reuters reported. Strikes late Thursday and early Friday hit Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kyiv, Kharkiv, and Chernihiv. Separately on Friday, the death toll from a Monday attack on an aid center in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia to 53, according to Ukraine's emergency service. Local police said earlier this week that as many as 39 people could still be trapped under the rubble. Indonesian police accuse a fourth official in alleged wiretapping of President Prabowo Subianto: In an investigation into the wiretapping of Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, police a fourth suspect on Friday, who they referred to by his initials, SU. Local media identified the suspect as Slamet Uliandi, who led the Criminal Investigation Agency's information and technology unit from 2021 to 2026. Earlier this week, police arrested three senior officers in connection with the wiretapping case, including Prabowo's chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo. Macau pro-democracy activist sentenced to 12 years in prison: A court in Macau, a special administrative region of China, the pro-democracy activist and former lawmaker Au Kam-san to 12-and-a-half years in prison on Friday. After a national-security trial that was held behind closed doors, Au, 69, was found guilty of "subverting state power by spreading false information" during Macau's leadership elections in 2024. The court said that he worked with "hostile organizations" abroad and leaked confidential information to overseas groups. Human Rights Watch condemned the sentence, and urged the European Union and Portugal, which formerly controlled Macau, to push for Au's release. Tanzania sentences opposition leader Tundu Lissu to four years in prison: On Friday, a three-judge panel in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, against Tundu Lissu, leader of the political opposition, convicting him of incitement for statements he made before the 2025 elections. The panel dropped a treason charge that carried a possible punishment of death. Lissu, the leader of the Chadema Party, called the trial "political persecution," and accused the judges of coordinating with the government. "I was not charged with incitement but you judges are convicting me with it just to impress the person who gives you the titles," he told the court. "I believe these were directives." He was arrested before the elections of October 2025, which the ruling President Samia Suluhu Hassan went on to win with 98% of the vote. His near-total victory prompted mass protests, which the government subdued by killing thousands of people, according to the political opposition and human-rights groups. British and EU lawmakers said that the case against Lissu was politically motivated and demanded his release. Egyptian soldiers killed in operation on Sudan border: Two Egyptian army officers were during a military crackdown on illegal gold mining along the border with Sudan, Reuters reported. One of the dead was a high-ranking officer. | | **You’re Invited: Bring the Kids! The Ice Age Comes Alive in Redwood City Saturday ** Join me this Saturday, November 7, for the plaque dedication and grand opening of the new HERO Natural History Gallery at the San Mateo County History Museum in Redwood City!

Bring your children and grandchildren to explore the Peninsula as it existed millions of years ago, discover the Ice Age animals that once roamed our region, see a reconstruction of a 15-million-year-old marine mammal and get up close to real mammoth and mastodon teeth! I'm especially proud to have championed a $500,000 Measure K grant to help make this exciting new gallery possible. I'll be joining museum officials and community members for the official unveiling at **1:30 p.m.** The free **History in Motion **celebration will also feature the opening of the spectacular Taube Family Carriage House and Automobile Gallery and Lora Mundi, the beautifully restored 1863 Lathrop-Connor-Mansfield House. **EVENT DETAILS** **When:** Saturday, November 7, 2026
**Time:** 1:30 p.m. – HERO Natural History Gallery unveiling
**Where:** San Mateo County History Museum
2200 Broadway, Second Floor Redwood City. I hope you'll bring the family and join us for this wonderful celebration! For more information, visit [https://historysmc.org](https://us.list-manage.com/16HY9qUKcgg?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02). Supervisor David J. Canepa
San Mateo County Board of Supervisors * * *

We KNOW we can win this race — but only if we have the resources to make sure that every single eligible Mississippi voter has had the opportunity to have their voice heard. body:
Thank you to our election workers. Virginia’s turnaround starts now.
| DELEGATE KAREN HAMILTON
---
Virginia House of Delegates, District 62
| Friends,
---
This election season asked a lot of all of us. I want to thank the many election and poll workers, and the volunteers who diligently worked throughout the year to fight for Virginia. Your long hours and steady commitment made a real difference.
It is an honor to serve the people of Virginia’s 62nd District, and this office belongs to you. Bills for next session are due at the end of this month. If you have a problem that a state law can solve, and you want to partner with our office on a solution, please fill out this form so we can begin the process.
| [Share Your Idea](https://hamiltonforvirginia.com/so/ccQ6jRq-l/c?w=1ko0zIaNUPAOfYp1ZUOHOsK3ZVKAEGH7ArBA3Y63PEQ.eyJ1IjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9kb2NzLmdvb2dsZS5jb20vZm9ybXMvZC9lLzFGQUlwUUxTZXhabnNvelc5SUs5NElaQndZbXpIaFM3Z3RCb0dpRHVkczRjZVJZVk5Tc2NWUXJ3L3ZpZXdmb3JtP3VzcD1oZWFkZXIiLCJyIjoiIiwibSI6Im1haWwiLCJjIjoiNDQyODg5MzMtZTRjYy00ZjEyLThmM2UtNmY0NWYzNzYyMWY0In0)

| JOIN ME AT THE RANGE

Freedom & Firearms Fundraising Event
After a tough election, join me at the gun range for food, fellowship, and firepower. The ammo is on me. The battle to turn Virginia around starts right now, and I need your help. Democrats want a super majority to destroy Virginia, and we’re not letting that happen. Stand with me.
| Thursday, November 12, 2026

Private facility on the south side of Culpeper
Tickets: $75 per person · Only 40 seats
| |

* * *
I spent most of yesterday bouncing from one media hit to the next, and I swear I heard the same question in almost every one. After Tuesday's historic night for Democrats, anchors and pundits kept leaning in with the same furrowed brow: _Aren 't you worried Democrats are going to overreach?_
I had to laugh. Because I don't remember a single person in the media asking Donald Trump and the Republican Party whether they were worried about overreaching after 2024. Not one.
In fact, I remember the opposite. I remember the press buying into a big lie: that Donald Trump won the 2024 election with a mandate. He didn't. It was an incredibly close election. If roughly 100,000 votes go differently across a handful of states, Kamala Harris is president right now. That's not a mandate. That's a coin flip that landed on its edge.
Now look at this week. Democrats just had their best midterm since 1974. We flipped as many as nine Senate seats. We flipped Texas. Texas!
_That_ is a mandate. And we earned it.
We earned it by nominating incredible candidates who rose above a bad party brand. They focused on the issues the American people told us mattered, they listened, and they were responsive. And voters were not subtle about what they wanted. Fix the economy, because everything costs too much and the job market sucks. End this war. Get rid of these tariffs. And go after the corruption that has rotted our government from the inside out.
So let's be clear about what overreach would actually look like. If Democrats walk in on day one, act like we're popular, and then say, "We're impeaching Donald Trump," that would be an extraordinary waste of time. Nobody voted for a political sideshow.
But that's not the choice in front of us, and the media knows it. What the American people want is for Democrats to call corruption and greed in Washington what they are: an affordability issue. Every dollar skimmed off the top by the people running this government is a dollar coming out of your pocket.
Take Elon Musk. The richest man in the world spent a fortune to buy his way into the government, then helped himself to the American taxpayer while gutting programs working families rely on. And he's not alone. There's Trump and his family's crypto schemes, Jared Kushner's investment fund, and the bribes people like Tom Homan and Alina Habba are taking. It's a whole administration treating the government like a cash register.
Expose it. Investigate it. Follow it with real legal action and prosecute these people to the fullest extent of the law. Then pass serious ethics and campaign finance reform. Start in the first week with a ban on insider trading in Congress and the White House. Make it bipartisan. Any Republican who claims to care about corruption can prove it with their vote, and Democrats should be just as eager to throw out the corrupt assholes in our own party. Then dare Donald Trump to veto it.
That's not overreach. That's the job. That's literally what the American people elected us to do. I'm tired of Democrats being held to a standard Republicans have never had to meet. That doesn't mean abandoning our principles or breaking the rules to get things done. It means playing the game, playing it hard, and actually using our power to make people's lives better.
And if you think I'm spinning, go back and look at what voters said after 2024. In focus groups and in polling, the message was the same over and over: Democrats mean well, but they can't get anything done. They're not fighting for _me_. They're fighting for somebody else.

* * *
I didn't see one word about overreach in any of the voter feedback I read. People weren't mad that we did too much. They were pissed that we didn't do enough. Pissed that we didn't transform the country. Pissed that we were focused on the wrong things. Pissed we didn't deliver on what we campaigned on.
So the time to deliver is now. This is a generational opportunity, and we cannot waste it being afraid of our own shadow.
Yes, Republicans will hide behind the filibuster. Yes, Donald Trump will veto a lot of bills. Fine. Make them own every vote. Make Trump own every veto. Then send this new crop of young, sharp, media-savvy Democrats across the country to tell people exactly who is standing between them and a better life. Ask voters for more Democratic senators, more Democrats in the House, and a Democratic president in 2028.
And shut out the noise. The Republicans and their MAGA media machine are going to scream about "lawfare." _It 's so unfair! They're coming after America's favorite president!_ Ignore them. Nobody cares. People want criminals investigated, exposed, and prosecuted, whether they're in the Epstein class, the Trump family, or the billionaire class.
And when the media decides we're "going too far," when they start parroting Republican talking points the way they did all day yesterday, tune them out. Stand on business. Stand on our values. That's what most Democrats did in this midterm, and it worked.
Deliver immediate, tangible improvements to the material conditions of people's lives. Take this country back from the corrupt cabal of genuinely evil people who have been abusing it and profiting off of it for far too long.
Voters already told us what they want. They didn't hand us this majority so we could be careful with it. They handed it to us so we'd finally use it.
Deliver. That's the whole strategy.
With urgency,
--Mike

name: Ken Martin
subject: I want to talk to you about trust today, Derek
body:
Democrats won because we earned back the trust of real people all over the country who are ready to see real change in their lives. [ ](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98055?t=1&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO)
---
Derek, it’s Ken Martin. I’m reaching out with a few thoughts and reflections as we end this historic week. **On Tuesday, all across the country, the American people put their trust in Democrats up and down the ballot, in what shaped up to be one of the most successful midterm elections in Democratic Party _history_.** It’s my mission as the chair of the Democratic National Committee to make sure that Democrats never take that trust for granted. I know I share that goal with the thousands of newly elected Democratic representatives across the country who are ready to create real change for the people in their states, districts, and communities. **Because Derek, none of the wins we saw on Tuesday were by chance. Democrats won because they have spent the past two years working overtime to earn back people’s trust.** In 2024, we faced a disillusioned public who felt like their government didn’t understand or stand for them. Democrats lost ground with communities we had relied on for decades, many of whom either voted Republican or stayed home. Since then, the DNC and Democrats nationwide have worked hard to repair those relationships by connecting with people on the ground — at their doors, on the phones, and in their communities. We made it a priority to _listen_ first, and to ask about what you wanted to see from your representatives. We didn’t wait until the few months before Election Day, we started our outreach the minute Trump took office. **And it worked.** In 2025, we saw major victories in states like Virginia, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania. _And importantly,**we didn’t stop showing up after Election Day.**_ Democrats in Virginia and New Jersey _got to work_ and passed meaningful statewide legislation to invest in affordable housing, deliver property tax relief, advance gun safety legislation, and secure funding to help people transition to cleaner energy sources. **And while Democrats in government got to work, Democratic candidates kept working around the clock to organize and talk to voters about what matters.** I am so proud of my team here at the DNC. On top of supporting over 10,000 Democratic campaigns this year, we also launched organizing initiatives, like _Local Listeners_ and _When We Count_ , to reach disillusioned Democrats who sat out last cycle and register _thousands_ of new Democratic voters. **Derek, it was because of innovative programs like these, and the hard work of campaigns and volunteers across the country, that Democrats were able to compete and win at _every level of government this Tuesday._** So I want us to take a moment and remember why this happened:_**People.** People who now have a sense that maybe, just maybe, some better days are ahead._ Democrats won because we earned back the trust of people all over the country who believe in us to deliver real change in their lives. **You — our grassroots team — made this possible. This victory belongs to all of you._But the work doesn’t end now._** Right now, newly-elected Democrats across the country are preparing to be sworn into office and get to work for their communities. And I want you to know that my team and I are listening to what folks are saying across the country — **we know that winning the White House in 2028 is dependent on Democrats delivering real change that Americans can _feel_ over the next two years.** We take seriously the level of trust that you’ve given us this year, and it’s time to continue building the depth of that trust with the way we govern. **That said, I also want to be clear about what my team is focused on, and that’s continuing to build on our winning infrastructure and investment strategies so that we can elect our next Democratic President and hold onto Congress.[If you’re ready and willing to support that effort, I hope you’ll consider chipping in a few bucks today. We’d be so grateful to have you on our team again.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261106_10248_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO) **[SUPPORT OUR WORK](https://ak.democrats.org/go/98376?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.YufugX&c1=7.SxDHGm&c2=em_20261106_10248_fr.47BODs&t=7&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO)** **If you can’t donate today, we understand, and we will continue working day in and day out to keep developing trust with grassroots Democrats like you, Derek.** Thank you again, for everything. We couldn’t have done it without you. Ken Ken Martin
Chair
Democratic National Committee | [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&amount=7&refcode=em_20261106_10248_fr&t=8&akid=10248%2E22930333%2EKT8yjO)
---

body:

---
**Thank You for Your Support PA-11**
Thank you...
To the voters of Lancaster and York Counties, our Democratic leadership, our state and congressional candidates, my campaign team and my family.
To our volunteers and everyone who contributed: you gave your time, your talents, and your heart. You knocked on doors, listened to neighbors, and helped turn a campaign into a community. **Our campaign shifted the PA-11 district 10.5 points toward Democrats as compared with the 2024 presidential election. We moved the needle - that 's no small feat and you should be proud of that!** Last night’s election result does not erase that progress, your work, or the connections we’ve built.
Here in Pennsylvania, the words “life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness” became part of our nation’s founding promise. Making that promise real in everyday life is the work of generations. It cannot begin or end with one election.
An election decides who holds office. It does not define our journey or the future of our democracy. The needs that you shared with me remain: a healthier economy, stronger schools, health care, immigration reform, support for farms and working people, and the freedom to make decisions about our bodies and whom we love. **These are reasons to keep working – not to walk away.**
This campaign is one chapter in a much longer effort to make government work for the people. That effort continues. The work ahead still matters: restoring trust and accountability, protecting the programs our communities depend on, and choosing compassion over cruelty.
Mending our country begins with listening to one another, especially when we disagree. Ask a neighbor what matters to them. Listen to understand – not just to answer. We can stand firmly for our values and still respect one another’s dignity. **Our differences do not change the fact that we are still neighbors.**
I implore you to keep showing up for your communities.
Volunteer, attend a community meeting, check on a neighbor, and make room for voices too often ignored. **We do not need to hold office to make a difference**. I will keep listening and showing up, and I hope you will join me.
Take a breath and take care of each other. Then, when you are ready, **stay involved**. Keep organizing, voting, **and holding elected leaders accountable**. Democracy is something we practice every day – not something that ends on election night.
Thank you for your courage, generosity, and belief that government should work for the people. **One loss does not end our movement. We will keep moving forward together**.
Thank you, Lancaster and York Counties. **Our work continues.**
\- Nancy Mannion

The slaughter of the Athenians at the Assinarus River by Syracuse in 413 B.C., as recorded by the historian Thucydides in his _History of the Peloponnesian War,_ is one of the best passages of human writing _._ The peerless Thucydides __ records the gruesome end of the Athenian era of empire with a visceral gore rivaled only by the macabre cannibalism of the Old Testament. The passage remains the most vivid depiction of the utter human despair and desperation brought about by war.
The great historian tells us the fleeing Athenians -- having foolishly overextended their military campaign into Sicily -- found themselves suddenly surrounded, driven back by a superior force, and exhausted into disorder by starvation and chaos. The anguished soldiers retreated helter-skelter and stumbled into the river. Forgetting the dire threat of the pursuing Syracusans, the hoplites hurled themselves into the river in a frenzy to quench their desperate thirst.
As the master historian conveys it:
> _When they reached the river, they plunged in with no order left. Each man wanted to cross first, while the enemy pressed them and made the crossing harder. Forced to move in a mass, they fell against one another and trampled one another down. Some were killed at once among the spears and equipment; others, tangled in it, were swept downstream. The Syracusans took positions on the far bank --which was steep--and shot down at the Athenians from above. Most of the Athenians drank eagerly, jostling one another in the hollow of the riverbed. The Peloponnesians came down after them and slaughtered chiefly those in the river. **The water was soon fouled, but even so they drank it, muddied and bloodied; many fought over it.**_
That is, so desperate was the plight of the routed Athenian army -- once an empire the envy of the Mediterranean world -- that its humiliated soldiers spent their dying moments slurping the blood of fallen comrades without thought of the murder raining down upon their heads.
Now... at the risk of sounding overly dramatic, the reason this passage comes to mind is because of the result of the elections. You need not have read much Thucydides to understand which political party is lying in puddles of blood and mire, electorally speaking.

Maine, in some ways, bucked the national trend. Now, this map could be the result of the tens of millions of dollars that flowed into the state on behalf of Susan Collins, but I'm choosing for the sake of my own self-esteem to believe that Maine's an outlier here because it's the only state with The Maine Wire conducting aggressive investigative reporting. That being said... the Maine GOP has been, once again, humiliated into despair.
As I write this, tens of thousands of lifelong Mainers -- Old Mainers, you might call them, irrespective of their age -- are eyeing the exits. Florida? New Hampshire? Tennessee? Is there somewhere you can run to where the schools won't be run for the benefit of corrupt teachers unions and transgender radicals? Is there another state that won't steal your money to enrich the friends and family of politicians, while simultaneously protecting organized crime and racketeering operations? Are there places where the cities aren't overrun with fentanyl-brained zombies, scaggy-armed with taxpayer-subsidized syringes, leaking their HIV-positive blood all over the children's playground?
Those who've placed Donald Trump at the center of their existence and allowed their hatred of him to animate their every impulse can be happy for a moment. But their lives aren't really going to change, except for perhaps they'll need something new to replenish their hatred in a few years. I'm sure J.D. Vance and Marco Rubio are up for the task. But for those who haven't been hanging out on overpasses wagging foreign flags, the question over every dinner table is whether Maine has crossed the socialist event horizon. That is, has Maine veered so close to the sucking black-hole maw of centrally planned corruption that there will be no reversing the economic, demographic, and cultural decline.
The answer to that question will depend, in large part, on the beleaguered conservative movement, if you can call it a movement. Those of the conservative disposition find themselves, once again, confused and leaderless, relegated to super minority status, destined to be ruled by DSA Democrats from the failed cities of Portland, Lewiston, and Bangor. We conservatives are like the Athenians, drowning in blood and mire, except we never even had a fond empire to remember, apart from the good ole days when Maine actually had an economy that wasn't wholly dependent on government spending and political patronage.
Whether the conservative movement can coalesce into a viable insurgency will become apparent over the next few weeks. Today, Republican senators and Republican House members will select leaders from their diminished ranks. Similarly, the chairman of the Maine Republican Party will appoint members of a nominating committee on Nov. 15, the beginning of the process that will determine whether current Maine GOP Chairman Jim Deyermond gets another two-year term. That party election will come in January, around the time the 133rd State Legislature is convening.

As the conservatives of Maine begin to navigate the next two years, it's worth looking back at the unlearned lessons of the past. To return to Thucydides:
> _It will be enough for me, however, if these words of mine are judged useful by those who want to understand clearly the events which happened in the past and which (human nature being what it is) will, at some time or other and in much the same ways, be repeated in the future._
In other words, Thucydides wrote and studied history primarily because human nature's immutability means that past events offer a preview into future events. What happened before is a guide to what will happen in the future. So with that as a starting point, we must begin by asking: What has happened within the Maine Republican Party that has produced such a miserable record of failure? How did Maine Republicans get wiped out by a party that has, over the last eight years, made life worse for Mainers by every conceivable metric?
The origin of our current predicament could be found in any of the post-LePage years. But I place it in the Covid-19 period, when the Republican Party ceded all manner of authority -- executive, moral, legal -- to Gov. Janet Mills. With all prudence cast aside, and federal Biden Bucks raining on Maine, Mills was able to buy off every pet constituency. That includes the no-bid contracts she used to secretly construct a political machine that would greatly aid in her re-election in 2022, as I've detailed at length with our reporting on Gateway Community Services.
As some of you may recall, in 2022, the consultants and campaign managers and analysts (all of whom make far more money than anyone at the Maine Wire) were predicting a "Red Wave." Commentator Phil Harriman predicted a full sweep for the red team, with 81 seats in the House, while then-BDN columnist and Maine Policy Institute CEO Matt Gagnon offered a slightly more measured view that there was a chance to flip the Senate. The nominal leaders of the Maine Republican Party were scheming and jockeying for who might become the Speaker of the House or the President of the Senate before the ballots had even been cast. I'm sure I was just as bullish -- or naive -- about the red wave, but I had the wisdom (or cowardice) not to write down any predictions.
Wrapped in the mirage that "she kept us safe," Mills defeated ex-Gov-now-Congressman Paul LePage -- both because LePage never directly assailed her totalitarian and unscientific pandemic policies and because he failed to articulate a sound abortion stance. Mills's second term, combined with an NGO complex constructed entirely on taxpayer money, made a formidable coalition. From 2020 to 2024, and perhaps still today, the gay race communists successfully harassed all good men and women out of politics with threats to ruin their lives or businesses for espousing crazy ideas like, maybe high school girls should not be forced to compete athletically against males who say they girls. So just as the Democratic machine was solidifying its formal political power, leftist cultural aggression sent conservatives into retreat.

Of course, 2022 was the first of several dismal performances for professional Republicans. The red wave was actually a red humiliation, with GOP candidates shellacked back into minority status here in Maine. Having just taken over TheMaineWire.com, I offered some candid observations about what I'd seen in the lead-up to the unexpected defenestration of the would-be Republican kings who were still measuring leadership office drapes by the time the polls started dousing them in reality. You can go back to the post-mortem I wrote in 2022 following that disastrous election. In that controversial piece of writing, I correctly predicted what Maine was about to experience over the next four years.
> [Gov. Janet] Mills could reverse course on her campaign promises, hike the income tax to 10 percent, encircle Swan's Island with offshore windmills, legalize fourth trimester abortion, and put a Planned Parenthood in every county, and I'm not sure Republicans in Augusta would be able to win majorities two years from now.
In fact, Gov. Mills and the Democratic majorities did raise our taxes, they did protect costly green energy scams, and they did impose the most extreme late-term infanticide law in Western Civilization. They imposed harsh gun control, expanded gender ideology into virtually every public space, and created an express superhighway for noncitizens to get welfare vis-a-vis the "Office of New Americans." Welfare fraud exploded almost exponentially while Asian transnational organized crime ran riot through rural Maine. Taxes soared and spending soared even more, leaving the Democrat coalition of the 133rd Legislature with a more than $1 billion deficit, which they will invariably tackle by hiking taxes even more on the handful of productive working people who've yet to escape this state.
My Jeremiah-like warnings fell on deaf ears. Here's the important point from four years ago that went ignored:
> The dwindling few Republicans who will inhabit the State House this next legislative session need a clean slate. Otherwise, they might as well spare taxpayers the per diem and stay at home. Anyone remotely connected to the old leadership must step back and allow a new generation of conservatives to lead the party. This includes staffers in the House and Senate GOP offices...
>
> I know the talent pool for Republican operatives is shallow in Maine, but we're at rock bottom here... As for new leadership, placing young, media savvy, strategically minded conservatives in charge is the only possible path to becoming relevant again...
None of this was particularly insightful or brilliant. After a professional football team goes multiple seasons without a single win, they typically change up the coach, the quarterback, and the strategy. But Republican leaders -- whoever those are or were -- did nothing of the sort. No new staff was hired. No new leaders were elevated. No new ideas or tactics were deployed. The same tired hands wrote the same tired scripts to blather out on the same AM radio signals to the same tired audience. Throughout the next legislative sessions, Republicans plowed through with the same perma-minority mindset that believes, falsely, that the extreme leftists who wear the Democrat name tags are interested in good-faith negotiations over policies that will improve the lives of Mainers. (Pro tip: They aren't.)
These leftist extremists who operate under the banner of the Maine Democratic Party are only interested in power, control, and money, with maybe a few naive youngsters still stupid enough to believe that "social justice" was ever a real thing. They will lie, cheat, and steal to get more power, control, and money, and you cannot negotiate in good faith with Democratic politicians and radicalized DSA staffers who will lie, cheat, and steal to advance their narrow, selfish interests. Yet, like Charlie Brown with the football, Republicans plodded ahead in the last three legislative sessions again and again for a kick, only to cry about sore asses on the House floor with speeches no one listens to and no one cares about. Meanwhile, Lucy snickers with her friends, counting stacks of cash, and chortling about stupid and gullible the conservatives.
That's not the only prescient wisdom I dispensed four years ago. Here's another bit:
> If a Republican donor wanted to make a substantial difference in future state elections, he should consider making a large donation only on the condition that it be used to construct an elite early voting and mail-in voting apparatus. Voting in modern elections now takes place over several weeks. Conservatives may not like it, it may open the door for fraud and bureaucratic shenanigans, but it's a reality. These are the rules and this is the playing field. If Republicans want to win, they must show up early, not just on game day.
Whether a GOP mega donor stepped up to the plate to fund such an effort, I don't know. Judging by the chronic indebtedness of the Maine Republican Party, I'm guessing no. Also: the results are right there in the early voting numbers. From 2022 to 2026, Republicans were clobbered in the early voting contest, even though they did make some slight progress in closing the gap. In 2022, Democrats had 64,622 more early voters than the Republicans did, a lead that dropped to 41,488 in 2026. However, Republicans managed to have 60,174 absentee ballot requests four years ago but just 31,618 this year. Very obviously, no concerted effort has been made to level the playing field in early voting. Trump bears most blame for this. His imbecilic pooh-poohing of early voting was a generational mistake. But he's not the only Republican with a platform. Who knows where the GOP might be sitting if they'd embraced some early voting initiatives, as conservative groups in other states have done so successfully. Indeed, if Republicans had embraced early voting with any kind of success, Democrats like Shenna Bellows might be out there condemning early voting as undemocratic!
Four years after my unheeded call for a better early voting program, I would also recommend that Maine conservatives embrace large-language models as a tool to help them fight from a minority and poorly financed position. Used properly, new and emerging technology could be the equivalent of giving the Mujahideen shoulder-fired rockets to take on the vastly superior Soviet forces. Of course, this would require them to listen to my earlier advice about hiring some staff who weren't already collecting Social Security when the Soviet Union was mucking around in Afghanistan. In case I haven't made myself clear, the GOP caucuses in the State House need to utterly gut the current staffer ranks and consultant ranks and come up with some brand new talent if they want anything to change. If they continue to pay the same staff and the same consultants, they will continue to get the same results.

The other area where the Maine Republican Party has seriously disadvantaged itself and must reform if it wishes to alter the trajectory of the state is structural and financial. Briefly, the Maine GOP's approach to raising and spending money is scattered and non-strategic. Compounding the problem, Republicans in Maine have a reputation among the donor class for being a group of greedy over-promisers who will both steal your money _and_ lose. Word spreads fast among GOP donors. One untrustworthy consultant or politician can create a negative feedback loop that leads to even good or worthy causes being ignored because of the perception that conservatives in Maine are not to be trusted. Earning back that trust will require a radical reformation of how the party operates.
Before explaining the money game at play in state politics, it's useful to understand a few things about how state legislative races are funded. Whether you like it or not, political campaigns require communicating ideas, and communicating ideas typically requires money. For both political parties, there are three principal political committees that endure regardless of individual personalities. These are used to raise money for the party state committees and legislative caucuses. On each side, there's the state committee, the state senate caucus committee, and the state house committee. Yes, there are dozens of other interest group funds and leadership PACs, but those are of less importance to this discussion than the big three central committees that set tone and strategy for party operations.
The most obvious fact that emerges from a cursory review of campaign finance documents is that the Maine Democratic Party and the Maine Republican Party are operated and governed according to completely different rules, philosophies, and strategies. The election results are the supreme judge of which party has the more effective mode of operation. Demonstrably, the Maine Democrats are running a more successful fundraising operation than the Republicans (which typically happens when a party can actually deliver legislation for pharmaceutical lobbies and other corporate interests), but the left-wing party is also much better at managing and deploying that cash to earn votes.
On the Democratic side, the House and Senate committees engage in regular fundraising. They wine and dine lobbyists, hold special events, and do the routine business of raising campaign cash. The expenditures are typically limited to the cost of fundraising: mail, payroll, office equipment, food and rent. But the key part is that eventually, a big chunk of the money raised by that committee is transferred to the central Democratic State Committee. The same goes for the Democratic Senate Committee. Regardless of who is running either political committee, the expenses are lean and all of the money flows to the central committee.
From 2018 through the available 2026 filings, the Democratic Senate and House committees reported payments to the state party of $10.51 million and $5.22 million, respectively, compared with $1.46 million and $216,640 from their Republican counterparts. The Democrats' current charter puts finances under a Finance Subcommittee and the annual budget before the Democratic State Committee. It also establishes a coordinated campaign committee for voter identification, absentee ballots, turnout, and voter files.
Once the money hits the central committee, the decisions about how to allocate that money are not made by a single chairman or executive director. Instead, the Democratic Party is governed by a committee so that many sets of hands and eyes have oversight over how campaign cash is being distributed. That's important for a few reasons. For one, it ensures that a shared and overarching strategic vision is overseeing the allocation of resources. That makes it less likely that a vulnerable incumbent will not get support or a candidate with a comfortable lead will get resources that could be spent elsewhere. Equally importantly, committee decision making over the allocation of resources ensures that campaign contributions are not steered for the benefit of narrow financial interests.
The spending mix is different, too. The campaign finance reports show Democrats reported $4.46 million for mailers and printed literature against Republicans' $1.47 million, and $4.65 million for payroll and staff against $1.41 million. Republicans reported $9.29 million for television and cable against Democrats' $1.93 million. That is a stark difference in what the committees bought. Of course, there's some overlap between the state campaign finance filings and the federal campaign finance filings, so these numbers aren't exactly perfect. But the records suffice to show significant differences in how the two parties raise, manage, and deploy resources.
The clearest way the Maine GOP could reform its various fundraising organs is by establishing governance via committee so that narrow interests can't dominate campaign spending in ways that are guided by something other than winning. Because let's face it: politics is a nasty game. It's even nastier behind the curtain with the consultants living that feast-or-famine lifestyle, hustling from election to election. Then you add to that the skim. For those who don't know, politics is filled with people who make money by skimming. They skim the fundraising. They skim the junk mail that clutters your mailbox and goes right in the garbage. They skim the television ads and the radio ads and the social media ads. A politician hires a fundraising consultant who helps him raise $500,000 for his campaign? Well, the fundraising consultant gets a slice of that treasure chest, even if all he did was provide a Rolodex and some talking points. Now, say that politician wants to spend $250,000 on television ads. Somewhere in the middle a political consultant is getting a skim -- could be 15%, 20%, or even more. Who's keeping track of that skim? Usually the one doing the skimming. But that's how political campaigns raise campaign cash and transform it into communications that reach voters.
There's nothing inherently wrong with the skim -- everyone has to eat -- but it does create perverse incentives to deploy resources in ways that prioritize something other than winning. For example, if you're getting the TV skim, you're probably going to recommend lots of TV. Ditto if you're getting the mail skim. If it turns out that paying young activists to door knock is the more effective strategy, but you're not getting a skim on the door-knocking... well, the door-knocking might get pushed to the back burner. Whoever emerges as the next crop of Republican leaders needs to take a careful look at who had been skimming and whether that skimming has been oriented toward the good of the party or toward narrower interests. Even if winning has been the top priority, a party that purports to back meritocracy ought to find a way to swiftly replace professionals with demonstrated losing records.
The last thing I'll say, at the risk of sounding too harsh on Maine's Republicans, considering that they're still drowning in their own blood and mire while spears and arrows rain down on their heads, is that they are vastly outmatched not only by a better funded and better run Democratic Party, but also by a humongous leftist dark-money operation that works hand-in-glove with official Democrats to advance the same goals, often in more vicious ways. I'm talking, of course, about the constellation of 501(c)3 and 501(c)4 and other NGOs funded by George Soros, Hansjorg Wyss, Pierre Omidyar, and many other leftist billionaires.
Unlike the Maine Republicans, the Maine Democrats have both the Bangor and Portland newspapers effectively serving as their communications and propaganda organs. And they have dozens and dozens of NGOs that get both dark-money funding _and_ taxpayer dollars. The playing field is tilted and the game is unfair. Conservatives can either whine about it, get better at politics, or move to New Hampshire.
